82350.e: Lake Oeschinen lies above Kandersteg. It is surrounded by high rock faces.

82351.q: Why are the mountains often reflected so beautifully in a mountain lake?
a: The water is calm and clear
The water is full of foam
The lake is made of glass
There are mirrors in the lake
82351.e: When there is no wind, the surface of the water is as smooth as a mirror. That is why you can see the mountains in it.

82352.q: What colour are some mountain lakes because of fine rock flour?
82352.e: Fine rock flour from glaciers floats in the water. It scatters the light, and the lake shines turquoise.
82352.m: Rock flour makes some mountain lakes turquoise.

82353.q: Which fish often lives in cold, clear mountain lakes?
82353.e: Trout like cold water with lots of oxygen. That is why they like living in mountain lakes and mountain streams.
82353.m: Trout like living in cold mountain lakes.

82354.q: Which mountain is a neighbour of the Dufourspitze and has a famous pyramid shape?
82354.e: The Matterhorn also stands near Zermatt. It is world famous for its pointed pyramid shape, but it is lower than the Dufourspitze.
82354.m: The Matterhorn is a neighbour of the Dufourspitze.

82355.q: Which pass do you take from Tiefencastel into the Upper Engadine to St Moritz?
82355.e: The road over the Julier Pass leads from Tiefencastel to Silvaplana in the Upper Engadine. From there it is not far to St Moritz.
82355.m: The Julier Pass leads into the Upper Engadine.

82356.q: In old legends, who threw the erratic boulders around the countryside?
82356.e: In the past, people did not know that glaciers had brought the stones. That is why legends told of giants or the devil throwing them.
82356.m: In old legends, giants threw the erratic boulders.

82357.q: Which plants often grow on a scree slope?
82357.e: On a scree slope there is little soil and the stones move. Only a few tough plants with long roots can grow there.
82357.m: Only a few tough plants grow on scree slopes.

82358.q: What is it called when water vapour cools and turns back into liquid water?
82358.e: When warm water vapour cools, little drops of water form again. This process is called condensation.
82358.m: In condensation, vapour turns back into water.

82359.q: What are the clouds in the sky made of?
a: Tiny drops of water and ice
82359.e: Clouds form when moist air rises and cools. This forms tiny drops of water or ice crystals.
82359.m: Clouds are made of very small drops of water or ice crystals.

82360.q: What are the drops of water that form on the grass early in the morning called?
82360.e: In the cool night, water vapour from the air turns into drops on the blades of grass. These drops are called dew.
82360.m: In the morning, dew often sparkles on the meadow.

82361.q: Why does a glass with an ice-cold drink get wet on the outside?
a: Water from the air settles on it
The glass has a tiny hole
The drink pushes through the glass
82361.e: The air contains invisible water vapour. On the cold glass it turns into drops.
82361.m: Drops of water from the air form on cold objects.

82362.q: Why do your glasses steam up in winter when you come into a warm house?
a: Warm, moist air cools on the cold lenses
The glasses get dirty in the house
The lenses go soft in the warmth
There is more dust in the house
82362.e: The glasses are still cold from outside. The warm room air cools on them, and its water vapour turns into tiny drops.
82362.m: Cold glasses steam up in a warm room.

82363.q: Why is the inside of the window panes often wet on cold winter mornings?
a: Moist room air cools on the glass
The cleaning cloth was too wet
82363.e: The warm air in the room contains water vapour. It cools on the cold pane, and drops form.
82363.m: Moisture collects on cold window panes.

82364.q: What are the white lines that aeroplanes draw high up in the sky called?
82364.e: The exhaust from the engines contains water vapour. In the freezing cold high up, it turns into tiny ice crystals that you see as lines.
82364.m: Condensation trails are made of tiny ice crystals.

82365.q: Why does water drip from the pipe of an air conditioner in summer?
a: Moisture from the air turns to water inside it
The unit is filled with water
The water comes from the rain
82365.e: In the air conditioner, the warm air is cooled down a lot. Its water vapour turns into water that has to drain away.
82365.m: When air cools a lot, its vapour turns into water.

82366.q: What is it called when water slowly turns into invisible vapour without boiling?
82366.e: Even without boiling, water particles are constantly passing into the air. This slow process is called evaporation.
82366.m: Water can evaporate even without boiling.

82368.q: Why do you feel cold when you climb out of the swimming pool wet?
a: The water on your skin evaporates and cools you
There are little bits of ice in the water
82368.e: Water needs heat to evaporate. It takes this heat from our skin, which is why we feel cold.

82369.q: Which cycle begins with water evaporating from seas and lakes?
82369.e: The evaporated water rises, forms clouds and falls back down as rain or snow. In this way the water keeps going round in a circle.
82369.m: In the water cycle, water travels between the earth and the sky.

82370.q: What provides most of the energy for water to evaporate from the sea?
82370.e: The sun warms the sea and the air. This makes a huge amount of water evaporate every day.
82370.m: The sun drives the evaporation of water.

82371.q: Why do people sometimes put a bowl of water on the radiator in winter?
a: To make the room air moister
82371.e: The warmth makes the water in the bowl evaporate. This puts more moisture into the dry heated air.
82371.m: Evaporating water makes dry air moister.

82372.q: How is salt obtained from seawater by the sea?
a: The water is left to evaporate in the sun
The water is shaken for a long time
The water is poured through a sieve
82372.e: In shallow pools, the sun and wind dry the seawater. The water goes into the air and the salt is left behind.
82372.m: When seawater evaporates, salt is left behind.

82373.q: How does a wet bath towel dry faster?
82373.e: Spread out, the towel has a large surface where water can go into the air. Scrunched up, it stays damp for a long time.
82373.m: A large surface makes water evaporate faster.

82374.q: On a high mountain, does water boil at more or less than 100 degrees?
a: It doesn't boil there at all
82374.e: On a mountain, less air presses down on the water. That is why it boils at a lower heat, for example at a mountain hut in the Alps.
82374.m: The higher you are, the sooner water boils.

82375.q: Which device do you use to measure how hot the water is?
82375.e: A thermometer shows the temperature. In Switzerland it is measured in degrees Celsius.
82375.m: You measure temperature with a thermometer.

a: The temperature at which something boils
The temperature at which something freezes
The highest point of a mountain
The point in the middle of the pan
82376.e: At the boiling point, a liquid starts to boil. For water at sea level, this is 100 degrees Celsius.
82376.m: At the boiling point, a liquid starts to boil.

82377.q: Who is the temperature unit degree Celsius named after?
82377.e: Anders Celsius was a scientist from Sweden. Almost 300 years ago he suggested a scale with 100 steps between water freezing and boiling.
82377.m: The Celsius scale is named after Anders Celsius.

82378.q: What happens to boiling water in an open pan if you turn the hob up even higher?
82378.e: The extra heat only makes more water turn to steam. But the temperature of the water does not rise above the boiling point.
82378.m: Boiling water does not get hotter, it just turns to steam faster.

82379.q: Why does water come to the boil faster with a lid on the pan?
a: The lid keeps the heat in the pan
The lid makes the water salty
The lid squeezes the water smaller
82379.e: Without a lid, a lot of heat escapes with the steam. With a lid, the heat stays in the pan, and you save energy too.
82379.m: With a lid, water boils faster and you save electricity.

82380.q: Which kitchen appliance boils water for tea especially quickly?
82380.e: In a kettle, a heating element warms the water directly. It switches itself off when the water boils.

82381.q: What is a pan with a tightly sealed lid, in which food cooks much faster, called?
82381.e: In a pressure cooker the steam cannot escape, so the pressure rises. This means the water only boils above 100 degrees, and the food cooks faster.
82381.m: It gets hotter in a pressure cooker than in an open pan.

82382.q: What happens to a puddle when it is minus 5 degrees outside?
82382.e: Minus 5 degrees is colder than the freezing point of water. That is why the puddle turns to ice.
82382.m: Below 0 degrees, a puddle turns to ice.

82383.q: Where in the kitchen do you keep food at about minus 18 degrees?
82383.e: A freezer keeps food at about minus 18 degrees. That way it keeps for a long time.
82383.m: It is much colder in the freezer than in the fridge.

82384.q: What are the balls of ice that sometimes fall from the sky in a thunderstorm called?
82384.e: In a thundercloud, drops of water freeze into balls of ice. When they fall, this is called hail.
82384.m: Hail is balls of ice from a thundercloud.

82385.q: Why should you never touch an ice-cold metal pole with your tongue in winter?
a: Your tongue can freeze to it
82385.e: The moist tongue cools down instantly on the ice-cold metal. The moisture freezes and the tongue sticks fast.

82386.q: What does it mean when the thermometer shows ‘minus 10 degrees’?
82386.e: The minus shows temperatures below zero. So minus 10 degrees is 10 degrees colder than 0 degrees.
82386.m: Minus degrees are colder than zero degrees.

82387.q: Why do people put antifreeze in the water for the car windscreen in winter?
82387.e: With antifreeze, the water only freezes at much lower temperatures. So you can clean the windscreen in winter too.

82388.q: What do you call it when rain freezes at once into a slippery layer of ice on the cold ground?
82388.e: When rain falls on ground colder than 0 degrees, it turns to ice at once. Then roads and pavements are very slippery.
82388.m: With black ice, the pavement is very slippery.

82389.q: What do you call weather with temperatures below 0 degrees?
82389.e: When it is colder than 0 degrees, we call it frost. Then water freezes outdoors.
82389.m: When there is frost, it is colder than zero degrees.

82390.q: Which three states can water have?
82390.e: Water can be solid as ice, liquid as water and a gas as steam. These are called states of matter.
82390.m: Water can be solid, liquid or gas.

82391.q: What state is an ice cube in?
82391.e: An ice cube is hard and keeps its shape. That is why it is solid.

82392.q: What state is water vapour in?
82392.e: Water vapour is a gas. It spreads out in the air and is invisible.
82392.m: Water vapour is water as a gas.

82393.q: What do you call it when ice turns into water?
82393.e: When ice gets warm, it becomes liquid. This process is called melting.
82393.m: When ice melts, it turns into water.

82394.q: What do you call it when a liquid becomes solid, for example hot wax?
82394.e: When a liquid cools, at some point it becomes solid. This process is called solidifying.
82394.m: When solidifying, a liquid becomes solid.

82395.q: What state is the lava that flows out of a volcano in?
82395.e: Lava is rock so hot that it flows. When it cools, it turns back into solid rock.

82396.q: What do you call it when water turns into steam while boiling?
82396.e: When boiling, liquid water quickly changes into a gas. This is called vaporising.
82396.m: When vaporising, a liquid turns into a gas.

82397.q: What shape are snowflakes when you look at them under a magnifying glass?
82397.e: Snowflakes are small ice crystals. They almost always have six arms or points.

82398.q: What happens to a blown-up balloon if you put it in the fridge?
82398.e: Cold air takes up less space than warm air. That is why the balloon shrinks a little.

82399.q: What can happen to a fully blown-up balloon in the hot sun?
82399.e: Warm air takes up more space. If the balloon is already full, the skin can tear.

82400.q: Why does an open balloon whizz around the room when you let go of it?
a: The air rushing out pushes it
It is pulled by the lamp
A gust of wind carries it
82400.e: The air rushes out of the back of the balloon. As it does, it pushes the balloon in the opposite direction. This is called recoil.
82400.m: Air rushing out drives a balloon forward.

82401.q: What are most balloons made of?
82401.e: Most balloons are made of rubber, or more exactly natural rubber. Rubber can stretch a lot.
82401.m: Balloons are made of stretchy rubber.

82402.q: Why does a balloon stick to the wall after you have rubbed it on your hair?
82402.e: When rubbed, the balloon gets an electric charge. This holds it to the wall.
82402.m: Rubbing gives a balloon an electric charge.

82403.q: Why does a helium balloon go limp after a few days?
a: The gas slowly escapes through the skin
82403.e: Helium particles are tiny. Little by little they slip out through the balloon skin.
82403.m: A helium balloon slowly loses its gas.

82404.q: Why does a balloon go bang when you prick it with a needle?
a: The air inside escapes all at once
82404.e: The air in the balloon is squashed together. When the skin tears, the air shoots out suddenly, and that makes the bang.
82404.m: A balloon goes bang because the air escapes suddenly.

82405.q: What happens if you blow up a balloon far too much?
82405.e: Rubber can only stretch up to a limit. If the skin gets too thin, it tears.
82405.m: A balloon blown up too much bursts.

82406.q: Why should you not leave bits of balloon lying around in nature?
82406.e: Birds, cows or wild animals sometimes mistake bits of balloon for food. This can make them ill.
82406.m: Bits of balloon belong in the bin.

82407.q: Which organ do we breathe with?
82407.e: Air goes through the nose or mouth into the lungs. There the oxygen passes into the blood.

82408.q: What do green plants give off into the air that we need to breathe?
82408.e: With the help of sunlight, plants make food from air and water. As they do, they give off oxygen, which we breathe in.
82408.m: Plants give off oxygen into the air.

82409.q: Why is the air we breathe out moist?
82409.e: In the lungs the air picks up moisture. That is why breathed-out air contains a lot of water vapour.

82410.q: Why should a classroom be aired regularly?
a: So that stale air gets out
So that the room gets darker
So that the floor gets clean
So that the lights shine brighter
82410.e: Lots of people in a room breathe out a lot of carbon dioxide. Airing lets fresh air in, and you can concentrate better.

82411.q: Through which part of the body is it best to breathe in, because it warms and cleans the air?
82411.e: In the nose the air is warmed and moistened. Tiny hairs hold back dust.
82411.m: The nose warms and cleans the air we breathe.

82412.q: What do divers need to be able to breathe underwater?
82412.e: A compressed air tank holds a lot of squashed-together air. The diver can breathe from it through a hose.
82412.m: Divers take their air with them in a tank.

82413.q: Which animal breathes underwater with gills?
82413.e: Fish take oxygen out of the water with their gills. Dolphins and whales, on the other hand, breathe air at the surface with lungs.

82414.q: What is the tube called through which the air we breathe goes from the throat to the lungs?
82414.e: The windpipe leads from the throat down to the lungs. The gullet next to it takes food to the stomach.
82414.m: The air we breathe flows through the windpipe.

82415.q: Which gas makes the bubbles in fizzy mineral water?
82415.e: Carbon dioxide is pressed into mineral water, or it is already in the spring water. In water it is often called carbonic acid.
82415.m: The bubbles in mineral water are carbon dioxide.

82416.q: What happens when you open a fizzy drink bottle that has been shaken?
82416.e: Shaking forms lots of gas bubbles. When you open the bottle, they escape all at once and carry water with them.
82416.m: Shaken fizzy bottles spray when opened.

82417.q: Why does mineral water taste flat if the bottle has been left open for a long time?
82417.e: The carbon dioxide gradually escapes into the air as a gas. Then the water no longer tingles.
82417.m: Open fizzy water loses its bubbles.

82418.q: Which of these drinks normally has no fizz?
82418.e: Cola, lemonade and sparkling water contain carbon dioxide. Milk does not fizz.

82419.q: Where does the fizz stay in the water longer?
82419.e: Cold water can hold more gas than warm. That is why a cool mineral water stays fizzy longer.
82419.m: Cold fizzy water stays bubbly longer.

82420.q: What do you hear when you open a fizzy drink bottle?
82420.e: In the closed bottle the gas is under pressure. When you open it, some of it rushes out with a hiss.
82420.m: A fizzy bottle hisses when opened.

82421.q: Is there spring water that is naturally fizzy?
82421.e: Some water takes up carbon dioxide deep underground. In Switzerland there are such springs, for example, in the Lower Engadine near Scuol.
82421.m: Some mineral springs are naturally fizzy.

82422.q: What is a device called that makes tap water fizzy at home?
82422.e: A sparkling water maker presses carbon dioxide from a gas canister into the water. This makes bubbles.
82422.m: With a sparkling water maker you can make fizzy water yourself.

82423.q: What does fizzy mineral water feel like in your mouth?
82423.e: The little gas bubbles burst on your tongue. You feel this as a tingle.

82424.q: What can a paper coffee filter take out of dirty water?
82424.e: Grains of sand are too big for the tiny holes in the paper. They get caught in the filter.
82424.m: A paper filter holds back sand.

82425.q: Can a paper filter take the salt out of salt water?
82425.e: Dissolved salt has broken up into tiny particles. These fit through every hole in the paper.
82425.m: Dissolved substances cannot simply be filtered out.

82426.q: Which layers are often used for a home-made water filter?
82426.e: The coarse gravel holds back big pieces, the sand smaller ones. The cotton wool catches the fine bits left over.
82426.m: Gravel, sand and cotton wool make cloudy water clearer.

82427.q: Which kind of carbon is found in many water filters?
82427.e: Activated carbon has a huge number of tiny pores. Smells and tastes get stuck to them.

82428.q: How is rainwater cleaned in nature before it becomes groundwater?
a: It seeps through gravel and sand
82428.e: On its way through soil, sand and gravel, a lot of dirt gets caught. The ground acts like a big filter.

82429.q: What is a plant called that turns lake water into drinking water?
82429.e: In a lake water works, water from the lake is filtered and cleaned. Zurich and Geneva, for example, get part of their drinking water this way.
82429.m: A lake water works turns lake water into drinking water.

82430.q: What does a tea strainer hold back?
82430.e: The hot water flows through the tiny holes. The tea leaves stay in the strainer.
82430.m: A tea strainer holds back the leaves.

82431.q: Why does a simple sand filter not make stream water safe to drink?
a: The sand makes the water salty
The water disappears into the sand
82431.e: A simple filter makes the water clearer. But it cannot reliably hold back very small germs.
82431.m: Clear water is not always clean drinking water.

82432.q: Which of these objects floats on water?
82432.e: Cork is very light and full of tiny air pockets. That is why a cork floats on top.
82432.m: A cork always floats on top.

82433.q: Why can a big steel ship float?
a: It is full of air inside
82433.e: A lump of steel would sink. But a ship is hollow and pushes aside a lot of water, so the water carries it.

82434.q: What helps small children stay up when learning to swim?
82434.e: Armbands are filled with air. They hold up the arms and so keep the child at the surface.

82435.q: What is the force with which water pushes things upwards called?
82435.e: Water pushes from below against everything in it. This force is called buoyancy.
82435.m: Buoyancy pushes things in water upwards.

82436.q: What happens if you shape a sinking ball of modelling clay into a flat little boat?
82436.e: As a boat, the clay pushes aside much more water. So the buoyancy is enough to carry it.
82436.m: Shape helps decide whether something floats.

82437.q: Why can you lie on the surface of the Dead Sea almost without moving?
82437.e: The Dead Sea contains much more salt than other seas. This water holds up the body especially well.
82437.m: In the Dead Sea you float like a cork.

82438.q: Which animals often have a swim bladder to hover in the water?
82438.e: Many fish have a gas-filled swim bladder in their belly. With it they hover in the water without sinking.
82438.m: The swim bladder helps fish hover.

82439.q: What does an apple do when you put it in a bucket of water?
82439.e: An apple contains a lot of air between its cells. That is why it floats on top.

82440.q: Why do children wear a life jacket on a boat?
a: It keeps their head above water
It protects them from the sun
82440.e: If you fall into the water, the life jacket holds you up. This keeps your head above the surface.
82440.m: A life jacket keeps you above water.

82441.q: What do you call a mixture in which a substance is completely dissolved in water?
82441.e: When sugar or salt has completely disappeared into water, a clear solution forms. You can no longer see any grains in it.
82441.m: A dissolved substance and water make a solution.

82442.q: Why can't you see dissolved sugar in water any more?
a: It has broken up into tiny particles
It has flown into the air
82442.e: The sugar is still there, but it has broken up into particles so small that you cannot see them.
82442.m: Dissolved sugar is invisible, but still there.

82443.q: What happens when you pour squash into water and stir?
82443.e: When stirred, squash spreads evenly through the water. The whole drink becomes sweet and coloured.

82444.q: What does water with a lot of salt dissolved in it look like?
82444.e: Dissolved salt particles are so small that light gets through. The salt water looks like normal water.
82444.m: Salt water looks like pure water.

82445.q: What is the liquid called in which a substance dissolves, for example water in sugar water?
82445.e: The water dissolves the sugar. That is why it is called a solvent.
82445.m: Water is the most important solvent.

82446.q: What happens to a sugar cube in cold water if you don't stir?
82446.e: The sugar dissolves even without stirring. But it takes much longer.
82446.m: Sugar dissolves even without stirring, just more slowly.

82447.q: Does a glass of water get heavier if you dissolve salt in it?
a: Yes, the salt is still in it
82447.e: The salt has only broken up into tiny particles. It is still in the water and weighs just as much as before.

a: Water with dissolved substances from leaves
82448.e: In hot water, colour, scent and flavour dissolve out of the leaves. The leaves themselves are left behind.
82448.m: Tea contains dissolved substances from leaves.

82449.q: Can you drink water from the tap in Switzerland?
82449.e: Tap water in Switzerland is strictly checked. You can drink it without worrying.
82449.m: Swiss tap water is good drinking water.

82450.q: What does the sign ‘Not drinking water’ on a fountain mean?
a: You should not drink the water
82450.e: At some fountains the water is not checked as drinking water. The sign warns you not to drink it.
82450.m: If it says ‘Not drinking water’, don't drink from the fountain.

82451.q: Why can't you simply drink seawater?
82451.e: Seawater contains a great deal of salt. If you drink it, you get even thirstier.
82451.m: Seawater is too salty to drink.

82452.q: Which Swiss city is known for over 1200 public fountains?
82452.e: The city of Zurich has over 1200 fountains. Fresh drinking water flows from most of them.
82452.m: Zurich is a city of fountains.

82453.q: Which drink is the best thirst quencher?
82453.e: Water quenches your thirst and has no sugar. Sweet drinks should only be drunk now and then.
82453.m: Water is the best thirst quencher.

82454.q: What is the water that comes out of the tap at home called?
82454.e: The water flows through pipes all the way to your home and out of the tap. That is why it is called tap water.
82454.m: Tap water comes out of the tap.

82455.q: What is the large store in which drinking water for a village is collected called?
82455.e: In the reservoir, clean drinking water is stored, often on a hill. From there it flows under pressure into the houses.

82456.q: What does it mean when people say the drinking water is ‘hard’?
a: It contains a lot of lime
82456.e: Hard water contains a lot of dissolved lime from the ground. You can see this from white marks in the basin or the kettle.
82456.m: Hard water contains a lot of lime.

82653.q: Who may read your diary if you do not allow it?
82653.e: A diary is part of your privacy. Nobody should read it without your permission.
82653.m: Nobody reads my diary without permission.

82654.q: How can you set who sees your posts in an app?
82654.e: In an app's settings you can often choose who may see something. Best of all, only friends and family.
82654.m: In the settings I decide who sees my things.

82655.q: What does “private” mean for a profile?
82655.e: A private profile can only be seen by people you have allowed. A public profile can be seen by everyone.
82655.m: Only my friends see a private profile.

82656.q: Is it OK to secretly look through another child's phone?
82656.e: Someone else's phone is part of their privacy. You always ask first.
82656.m: I only look at other people's phones with permission.

82657.q: What does “public” mean on the internet?
82657.e: Anyone on the internet can see public posts, strangers included.

82658.q: What should a child do if a game asks for their location?
82658.e: Your location shows where you are right now. Ask your parents first whether the game really needs it.
82658.m: When asked for my location, I ask my parents first.

82659.q: Who else can see a message that you send to lots of people?
82659.e: Anyone who gets a message can read it and forward it. That is why you think carefully first.
82659.m: All the recipients can read a message I send.

82660.q: Can the internet definitely forget something for ever when you delete it?
82660.e: Others may already have copied or saved something before you delete it. That is why the rule is: think first, then post.
82660.m: The internet does not forget so quickly.

82661.q: Which of these is a piece of personal data?
82661.e: Personal data tells something about you as a person. Your address shows where you live.
82661.m: My address is part of my personal data.

82662.q: Who do you give your phone number to on the internet?
82662.e: Your phone number is personal data. Strangers on the internet should not get it.
82662.m: I do not give my phone number to strangers.

82663.q: Which of these is more OK to show in a game?
82663.e: A made-up name says nothing about you. School, address and date of birth are personal data.
82663.m: A made-up name protects me in a game.

82664.q: Why should you not post the name of your school publicly?
82664.e: Anyone who knows the name of your school knows where you are during the day. That is none of a stranger's business.
82664.m: I do not post the name of my school publicly.

82665.q: What do you do if a website asks for your name and address?
82665.e: With personal data you ask your parents first. They know whether the site can be trusted.
82665.m: Before typing in my details, I ask my parents.

82666.q: Which photo gives away where you live?
a: In front of the house with the house number
82666.e: In a photo in front of your house, people might see the street and house number. That way someone could find out where you live.
82666.m: Photos can give away my address too.

82667.q: What is a secret you do not pass on when logging in?
82667.e: The password protects your account. Only you and your parents should know it.

82668.q: Who often collects data about you on the internet?
82668.e: Many apps and websites save what you click on and type in. That is why you give away only a little.
82668.m: Apps and websites often collect data.

82669.e: You use your username to log in to a game or an app. Others often see it.
82669.m: I log in with my username.

82670.e: “StarFox” says nothing about you. The others show a name, home town or address.
82670.m: A good username says nothing about me.

82671.q: What should a username not contain?
82671.e: Your full name is personal data. With it, strangers can find you more easily.
82671.m: My full name does not belong in my username.

82672.q: Why is your year of birth in a username not a good idea?
82672.e: A year like 2017 shows how old you are. Strangers do not need to know that.
82672.m: My age does not belong in my username.

82673.q: What is the difference between a username and a password?
82673.e: Others often see your username. The password, however, stays secret.
82673.m: The username is visible, the password stays secret.

82674.q: What do you call a small picture next to the username?
82674.e: The profile picture appears next to your name. Instead of a photo of yourself, it is better to use a picture or a character.
82674.m: For my profile picture I prefer a character.

82675.q: Who should help you think up a username?
82675.e: Parents help you find a safe name without personal data.
82675.m: My parents help me with my username.

82676.q: Which username gives away where you live?
82676.e: “Noah_Thun” shows the first name and the town of Thun. The other names give nothing away.
82676.m: A place name in my username gives away where I live.

82677.q: Do you know for sure who is behind a profile on the internet?
82677.e: On the internet people can use a fake photo and a fake name. That is why you never know for sure.
82677.m: On the internet anyone can pretend to be someone else.

82678.q: A stranger in a game wants to meet you. What do you do?
82678.e: Never meet people from the internet on your own. Tell your parents or another adult straight away.
82678.m: I talk to my parents about meeting strangers from the internet.

82679.q: A stranger writes: “This is our secret.” What do you do?
82679.e: Good friends do not ask you to keep secrets from your parents. Tell an adult you trust.
82679.m: I tell an adult about strange secrets.

82680.q: A stranger offers you presents in a game. What do you do?
a: Say no and tell your parents
82680.e: Strangers offering presents often want something back. Say no and talk to your parents.
82680.m: I refuse presents from strangers on the internet.

82681.q: Which function lets you block an unpleasant player?
82681.e: With “Block” the person can no longer write to you.

82682.q: What does the “Report” function do in an app?
a: It informs the people who run the app
82682.e: With “Report” you tell the people who run the app that someone is behaving badly. They can block that person.
82682.m: By reporting, I help make the app safer.

82683.q: Who may a child write to in a chat?
82683.e: It is safest to write only to people you also know in real life.
82683.m: I chat with people I really know.

82684.q: A stranger asks: “Are you home alone?” What is right?
82684.e: That is none of a stranger's business. Do not answer and tell your parents.
82684.m: I do not answer strangers' questions about my home.

82685.e: A chain letter tells you to forward the message to lots of other people.
82685.m: A chain letter wants me to pass it on.

82686.q: A chain letter threatens: “Send this on, or something will happen to you!” Is that true?
a: Yes, if you have read it
82686.e: Threats like that are made up. Nothing happens if you do not forward the chain letter.
82686.m: Threats in chain letters are made up.

82687.q: What is the best thing to do with a chain letter?
82687.e: You simply delete the chain letter. That way the chain stops with you.

82688.q: What do you do if a chain letter scares you?
82688.e: Talking to your parents or a teacher helps against the fear. They explain that the letter is not true.
82688.m: If a chain letter scares me, I talk to an adult.

82689.q: Why do chain letters reach so many people so quickly?
a: Everyone sends them to lots of people
82689.e: If everyone forwards to lots of people, the number of recipients grows very quickly.
82689.m: Chain letters spread because lots of people forward them.

82690.q: A chain letter promises good luck if you forward it. Is that true?
a: Yes, if you send it to ten people
Yes, if you send it quickly
82690.e: A chain letter cannot bring luck. The promise is only meant to make you forward it.
82690.m: Chain letters do not bring luck.

82691.q: Who has usually written a chain letter?
82691.e: You usually do not know who made up a chain letter. It has just been forwarded many times.
82691.m: You usually do not know who sent a chain letter first.

82692.q: What is a warning sign in a chain letter?
82692.e: Chain letters often threaten you or put you under time pressure. That is how you recognise them.
82692.m: Threats and time pressure are warning signs.

82693.q: Why do many free apps show adverts?
82693.e: Free apps often earn money with adverts. Companies pay for you to see the adverts.
82693.m: Free apps often earn money with adverts.

82694.q: A window flashes: “You have won! Click here!” What do you do?
82694.e: Prize messages like that are almost always tricks. You do not click them and you close the window.
82694.m: I do not click on fake prize messages.

82695.q: How can you often recognise adverts on the internet?
82695.e: Adverts are often marked with “Ad”, “Advertisement” or “Sponsored”.
82695.m: Adverts are often labelled with the word Ad.

82696.q: What is an influencer doing who praises a toy and gets money for it?
82696.e: If someone gets money or presents for praising a product, that is advertising.

82697.q: What is the safest way to close a pop-up advert?
82697.e: The small X at the top usually closes the window. Big colourful buttons often lead to more adverts.
82697.m: I close pop-up adverts with the small X.

82698.q: What is a short advertising film, for example before a video, called?
82698.e: An advert is a short film that praises a product. You see it on television or before videos on the internet.
82698.m: An advert is a short advertising film.

82699.q: Is everything adverts promise really true?
82699.e: Adverts show products looking especially good. In real life they are often smaller or less great.
82699.m: Adverts often show things looking better than they are.

82700.e: With an in-app purchase you pay inside a game or app, for example for coins or characters.
82700.m: An in-app purchase costs real money.

82701.q: Does a free app sometimes cost money after all?
82701.e: Many free apps sell extras inside the game. These cost real money.
82701.m: Free apps can cost money too.

82702.q: What do you do before you buy something in a game?
82702.e: You may only buy something with your parents' permission. It is real money.
82702.m: Before every purchase I ask my parents.

82703.q: Game coins cost 5 francs in the game. Is that real money?
82703.e: If you buy game coins with francs, you pay with real money. The money is gone afterwards.

82704.q: How can parents prevent in-app purchases?
82704.e: In the settings you can protect purchases with a password or a lock.
82704.m: A purchase lock protects against unwanted purchases.

82705.q: You buy 3 packs for 2 francs each. How much does that cost?
82705.e: 3 packs times 2 francs is 3 times 2, so 6 francs.
82705.m: Three times two francs makes six francs.

82706.q: A game says: “Only 1 minute left! Buy now!” What does it want?
82706.e: With time pressure the game wants you to buy quickly without thinking.
82706.m: Time pressure is meant to make me buy quickly.

82707.q: What is a surprise box in a game that you can buy called?
82707.e: A loot box is a surprise box. You do not know beforehand what is inside, but you pay anyway.
82707.m: With a loot box you do not know what you will get.

82708.q: What does an age rating on a game show?
a: From what age it is suitable
82708.e: The age rating says from what age a game or film is suitable.
82708.m: The age rating shows from what age something is suitable.

82709.q: Which age rating is suitable for a 7-year-old child?
82709.e: PEGI 7 means suitable from age 7. The other games are for older children or adults.
82709.m: PEGI 7 is suitable from age seven.

82710.q: What is the lowest PEGI age rating?
82710.e: PEGI 3 is the lowest rating. Games like that are fine even for small children.

82711.q: Which PEGI rating is only for adults?
82711.e: PEGI 18 means only from age 18. These games are for adults.

82712.q: Where do you find a game's age rating?
82712.e: The age rating is on the packaging and in the app store with the description.
82712.m: The age rating is on the packaging.

82713.e: Some games and films can frighten or overwhelm children. Age ratings protect them from that.

82714.q: A game is rated PEGI 12. May an 8-year-old child play it?
82714.e: PEGI 12 means only from age 12. A child of 8 is too young for it.
82714.m: For PEGI 12 you have to be at least twelve.

82715.q: How many years does a 9-year-old child still need to wait for PEGI 12?
82715.e: You calculate 12 minus 9. That makes 3 years.
82715.m: At nine, there are three years to go until PEGI 12.

82716.q: What do you do if you are treated meanly in the class chat?
82716.e: Get help from your parents or teachers. Insulting back usually makes it worse.
82716.m: If I am cyberbullied, I get help.

82717.q: Why should you not delete mean messages straight away?
82717.e: A screenshot of the messages serves as evidence. That way adults can help better.
82717.m: I save mean messages as evidence.

82718.q: Can cyberbullying happen in the evening and at the weekend too?
82718.e: Your phone is almost always with you. That is why cyberbullying can happen at any time, even at home.
82718.m: Cyberbullying can happen at any time.

82719.q: What do you do if you see someone else being picked on online?
82719.e: Bystanders can help too, by telling adults. Laughing along makes the bullying bigger.
82719.m: If others are being picked on, I get help.

82720.e: “Well done!” is kind. The other sentences hurt.
82720.m: On the internet I stay friendly.

82721.q: How does someone who is being bullied feel?
82721.e: Bullying hurts. People affected often feel sad, alone or afraid.

82722.q: Which rule applies on the internet just like in the playground?
82722.e: On the internet there are real people behind the screens. That is why respect matters there too.
82722.m: I am respectful on the internet too.

82723.q: Which telephone number helps children and young people in Switzerland with worries?
82723.e: The number 147 is the advice line for children and young people. The other numbers are emergency numbers.

82724.q: How much does a call to the number 147 cost?
82724.e: The advice line 147 is free. That way every child can call.

82725.q: Which foundation runs the advice line 147?
82725.e: The advice and help line 147 belongs to the foundation Pro Juventute.
82725.m: The number 147 belongs to Pro Juventute.

82726.q: Besides by phone, how can you reach the advice line 147?
82726.e: With 147 you can not only call, but also chat or write an email.

82727.e: The number 147 is there especially for children and young people.
82727.m: 147 is there for children and young people.

a: Only if there is a fire
82728.e: At 147 you can talk about anything that worries you, for example arguments, bullying or fear.
82728.m: At 147 I can talk about any worry.

82729.q: Which number do you dial if there is a fire?
82729.e: If there is a fire, you call the fire brigade on 118. 147 is there for worries and questions.

a: A message that is not true
82730.e: Fake news tells you something that is not true but looks real.
82730.m: Fake news looks real but is not true.

82731.q: What are false reports on the internet often called?
82731.e: False reports are called fake news. “Fake” means forged or not real.

82732.q: What do you do before you forward an amazing message?
82732.e: Before sharing, you ask adults or look it up in reliable sources.

82733.q: Where are you more likely to find correct news for children?
82733.e: Children's news on television or online is checked by experts.

82734.q: How can you often recognise fake news?
82734.e: Fake news often causes fear or anger, so that people forward it quickly.
82734.m: Fake news often wants to scare me.

82735.q: What is the source of a piece of news?
82735.e: The source shows who wrote a piece of news and where it comes from. Well-known sources are usually more reliable.
82735.m: With news, I look at the source.

82736.q: Who do you ask if you do not know whether a piece of news is true?
82736.e: Parents or teachers help you check whether a report is true.
82736.m: If I am in doubt, I ask an adult.

82737.q: What happens when lots of people share fake news?
82737.e: The more people share fake news, the more people believe it. But that does not make it true.
82737.m: Sharing fake news does not make it true.

82738.q: A friend sends you a photo of a child so you can laugh at them. What do you do?
a: Use it as your profile picture
82738.e: A photo meant for laughing at someone hurts that child. You do not forward it and you talk to an adult.
82738.m: I do not forward photos meant to laugh at someone.

82739.q: What is the right to decide about photos of yourself called?
a: The right to your own image
82739.e: The right to your own image means you decide whether a photo of you is shown.
82739.m: I have the right to my own image.

82740.q: Can you simply pass off a photo from the internet as your own?
82740.e: Whoever took a photo has rights to it. You do not pass it off as your own.
82740.m: I do not pass off other people's photos as my own.

82741.q: When is the best time to post holiday photos?
a: On the first day of the holiday
82741.e: Posting during your holiday shows everyone that nobody is at home. That is why it is better to wait until you are back.
82741.m: I only post holiday photos after the holiday.

82742.q: What do you do if someone shows an embarrassing photo of you?
82742.e: Adults can help get the photo deleted. You do not have to sort it out on your own.
82742.m: With embarrassing photos, I get help.

82743.q: May you secretly post a funny photo of your teacher?
82743.e: Teachers also have the right to their own image. You do not post it without permission.
82743.m: I only post photos of others with permission.

82744.q: Who is it best to send photos of yourself to?
82744.e: You only send photos to family and real friends. Strangers should not get photos of you.
82744.m: I only send photos of me to people I know.

82745.q: What can the background of a photo give away?
82745.e: In the background you often see street signs, buildings or the school. That way people know where you are.
82745.m: The background of a photo can give something away too.

82746.q: Which of these is not personal data?
82746.e: Everyone knows the capital, Bern; it says nothing about you. Birthday, mobile number and address are personal data.
82746.m: Personal data tells something about me.

82747.q: May you use a friend's username to pretend to be them?
82747.e: Pretending to be someone else is unfair and can harm them. Everyone uses only their own account.
82747.m: I only use my own account.

82748.q: A stranger wants you to switch to another app to chat privately. What do you do?
a: Say no and tell your parents
82748.e: Someone who wants to lure you into another app often wants nobody else to read along. Say no and tell your parents.
82748.m: I do not switch to other apps with strangers.

82938.q: What cushions knocks in the knee like a little pillow?
82938.e: The meniscus is a crescent-shaped disc of cartilage between the thighbone and the shinbone. It cushions knocks when walking and jumping.
82938.m: The meniscus cushions knocks in the knee.

82939.q: How many menisci does each knee have?
82939.e: Each knee has an inner meniscus and an outer meniscus. So together there are two.

82940.q: What are the ligaments called that cross like an X in the middle of the knee joint?
82940.e: In the knee there is a front and a back ligament that cross over each other. They stop the lower leg sliding away forwards or backwards.
82940.m: The cruciate ligaments keep the knee stable.

82941.q: What does your knee joint do when you ride a bike?
82941.e: When pedalling, the knee is bent and straightened again and again. That is why cycling is good exercise for the knees.
82941.m: When cycling, the knee bends and straightens again and again.

82942.q: What do you call legs where the knees touch but the feet are apart?
82942.e: When the knees come together inwards, the legs look like the letter X. In small children this is often normal and grows out.
82942.m: With knock knees, the knees touch.

82943.q: What do you call legs with a large gap between the knees?
82943.e: The legs then form a round shape together like the letter O. Many babies have slightly curved legs that later become straight.
82943.m: With bow legs, the knees are far apart.

82944.q: When can you turn your lower leg a little at the knee?
a: When the leg is fully straight
Never, the knee is purely a hinge
82944.e: When the knee is bent, the ligaments are a little looser, so the lower leg can turn slightly. When the leg is straight, the knee is firm and stable.
82944.m: Only with a bent knee can you turn your lower leg a little.

82945.q: How do you land after a jump in the way that is kindest to your knees?
82945.e: Bent knees cushion the impact like a spring. With stiff legs, the whole jolt goes into the joints.
82945.m: After a jump, land with slightly bent knees.

82946.q: What do people often wear after a knee injury to support the knee?
82946.e: A knee support fits tightly around the knee. It supports the joint and gives stability when walking.
82946.m: A support helps an injured knee.

82947.q: What does the doctor do when a shoulder is dislocated?
a: She puts it back in place
She sticks a plaster on it
82947.e: With a dislocated shoulder, the bone has slipped out of the joint. The doctor carefully pushes it back.
82947.m: A dislocated shoulder is put back in place.

82948.q: Which large joint pops out of its socket most often?
82948.e: The shoulder is very mobile but not as firmly built as other joints. That is why it dislocates more easily in a fall.
82948.m: Of all the large joints, the shoulder dislocates most often.

82949.q: Why can you move your shoulder so far in all directions?
a: The socket is small and flat
The socket is deep and narrow
The joint has many ligaments made of bone
The joint is a hinge joint
82949.e: The round head of the upper arm bone sits in only a small, flat socket. So it has plenty of room to move.
82949.m: The flat socket makes the shoulder very mobile.

82950.q: Which bone forms the socket of the shoulder?
82950.e: There is a small hollow on the shoulder blade. The head of the upper arm bone sits in it.
82950.m: The shoulder socket belongs to the shoulder blade.

82951.q: Which bone sits with its round head in the shoulder joint?
82951.e: The upper arm bone has a round head at the top. This head moves in the shoulder joint.
82951.m: The head of the upper arm bone sits in the shoulder joint.

82952.q: What mainly holds the upper arm bone in place in the shoulder?
82952.e: Strong muscles and tendons surround the shoulder joint. They hold the upper arm in place like a cuff.
82952.m: Muscles and tendons hold the shoulder together.

82953.q: What do you need to lift your arm up?
82953.e: Strong muscles lie over the shoulder. They pull the arm up, to the side and forwards.

82954.q: What is a good way to warm up your shoulders before sport?
82954.e: With arm circles, the shoulder joint moves in all directions. That way the muscles and joint get warm and ready for sport.
82954.m: Arm circles warm up the shoulders.

82955.q: Which joint do you mainly move when you put your hand up at school?
82955.e: When you put your hand up, you lift your whole arm above your head. This movement is done mainly by the shoulder.
82955.m: Putting your hand up mainly moves the shoulder.

82956.q: What is the hollow in the pelvis called, where the top end of the thighbone sits?
82956.e: The hip socket is a deep hollow in the pelvic bone. The head of the thighbone turns in it.
82956.m: The thighbone sits in the hip socket.

82957.q: Why can you move your leg at the hip less far than your arm at the shoulder?
a: The hip socket is very deep
The hip is made of cartilage
82957.e: The head of the thighbone sits deep in the hip socket. This makes the hip very stable but a bit less mobile.
82957.m: The deep hip socket makes the hip stable.

82958.q: What do older people sometimes get when their hip joint is badly worn?
82958.e: A worn hip joint can be very painful. Doctors can replace it with an artificial joint made of metal and plastic.
82958.m: A worn hip joint can be replaced with an artificial one.

82959.q: What does the hip joint connect?
82959.e: In the hip joint, the thighbone sits in the pelvis. That way the leg is connected to the body and can move.
82959.m: The hip joint connects the leg to the pelvis.

82960.q: Which joint do you bend when you pull your knee up high to your chest while marching?
82960.e: When the whole leg goes up forwards, the hip bends. It connects the leg to the pelvis.
82960.m: The hip bends when you lift your leg forwards.

82961.q: Which toy do you keep spinning around your tummy by circling your hips?
82961.e: With a hula hoop you move your hips quickly back and forth. That way the hoop stays up and spins around your body.
82961.m: Circling your hips keeps a hula hoop going.

82962.q: Which joints carry the weight of the whole upper body when you stand?
82962.e: The upper body rests on the pelvis. From there the weight goes through the hip joints into the legs.
82962.m: The hip joints carry the weight of the upper body.

82963.q: How many hip joints does a person have?
82963.e: Each leg is attached to the pelvis by its own hip joint. So there is a left and a right hip joint.

82964.q: How many joints does an index finger have, not counting the wrist?
82964.e: The index finger has three finger bones. Between them and at the hand there are three joints altogether.
82964.m: An index finger has three joints.

82965.q: How many finger bones does the thumb have?
82965.e: The thumb is shorter than the other fingers. It has only two finger bones; the other fingers have three.
82965.m: The thumb has two finger bones.

82966.q: Why is it harder to move your fingers when it is very cold?
a: Cold muscles and tendons get stiff
82966.e: In the cold, muscles and tendons become less supple. If you warm up your hands, your fingers can move easily again.
82966.m: Cold fingers are stiff and warm fingers move easily.

82967.q: What is the finger joint right at the front, by the fingertip, called?
82967.e: It is called the end joint because it is at the end of the finger. With it you bend only the fingertip.
82967.m: The front finger joint is called the end joint.

82968.q: What is the finger joint called where the finger joins the hand?
82968.e: This joint is at the base, that is the start, of the finger. There the finger is connected to the middle of the hand.
82968.m: Where the finger starts at the hand is the base joint.

82969.q: In which direction do the finger joints bend easily?
a: Towards the back of the hand
82969.e: The finger joints work like little hinges. They bend towards the palm, so you can make a fist.

82970.q: How do you often sprain a finger when playing ball games?
82970.e: If the ball hits the straight fingertip, a joint gets jammed. This often happens in volleyball or basketball.
82970.m: A ball hitting the fingertip can injure a finger joint.

82971.q: What are the hard bumps on the back of the hand called, which you see when you make a fist?
82971.e: When you make a fist, the base joints of the fingers stick out as bumps. They are called knuckles.
82971.m: You see your knuckles when you make a fist.

82972.q: What is the joint between the lower leg and the foot called?
82972.e: The joint of the foot is called the ankle joint. You need it to walk, run and jump.
82972.m: The joint of the foot is called the ankle joint.

82973.q: What are the two hard bumps on the left and right of the ankle called?
82973.e: At the ankle there is an inner and an outer ankle bone. They are the ends of the two lower leg bones.
82973.m: You can feel an ankle bone on the inside and outside of the ankle.

82974.q: Which ligaments of the ankle are most often injured when you go over on your ankle?
82974.e: Usually the foot turns inwards, so the outer side is overstretched. That is why the ligaments on the outside of the joint get injured.
82974.m: When you go over on your ankle, the outer ligaments usually suffer.

82975.q: What does the ankle joint do when you stand on tiptoe?
82975.e: On tiptoe, the foot points downwards. The ankle joint makes this movement together with the calf muscles.
82975.m: On tiptoe, the ankle points the foot downwards.

82976.q: Which shoes protect the ankle especially well when hiking in the mountains?
82976.e: High hiking boots reach over the ankle and give it support. That way you are less likely to go over on your ankle on stony paths.
82976.m: High hiking boots support the ankle.

82977.q: What is the thick tendon at the back above the ankle, which runs to the heel, called?
82977.e: The Achilles tendon connects the calf muscles to the heel bone. It is the strongest tendon in the body.
82977.m: The Achilles tendon runs to the heel.

82978.q: Which exercise can strengthen your ankles?
a: Lying down for a long time
82978.e: When balancing, many small muscles around the ankle work. This makes it more stable, and you are less likely to go over on it.
82978.m: Balancing on one leg strengthens the ankles.

82979.q: What helps first when your ankle swells up after you go over on it?
a: Cooling it and raising the foot
82979.e: Cold and a raised foot make the swelling less bad. Then an adult should check whether it needs a doctor.
82979.m: Cool a twisted ankle and raise it.

82980.q: Why should you not yank small children up by their hands and swing them around?
82980.e: In small children, strong pulling can make a bone at the elbow slip out of place. This hurts, and the child no longer wants to move the arm.
82980.m: Never pull small children by the arms with a jerk.

82981.q: How many bones meet in the elbow joint?
82981.e: In the elbow, the upper arm bone meets the two forearm bones, the ulna and the radius. That makes three bones.
82981.m: Three bones meet in the elbow.

82982.q: Which muscle on the back of the upper arm straightens the elbow?
82982.e: The triceps is at the back of the upper arm. When it contracts, the arm straightens at the elbow.

82983.q: Which movement does the elbow allow, apart from bending and straightening?
82983.e: In the elbow, the radius can turn around the ulna. That way you can turn your palm up or down.
82983.m: Thanks to the elbow, you can turn your forearm.

82984.q: Where does it hurt with ‘tennis elbow’?
a: On the outside of the elbow
On the sole of the foot
82984.e: With tennis elbow, tendons on the outside of the elbow are overloaded. It can also happen without tennis, for example from lots of work with a computer mouse.
82984.m: Tennis elbow hurts on the outside of the elbow.

82985.q: Apart from a helmet, which protection is important for your arms when skateboarding?
82985.e: When you fall, you often land on your elbows. Padded protectors protect the skin and the joint.
82985.m: Elbow pads protect your arms when skateboarding.

82986.q: How far can you straighten your arm at the elbow?
82986.e: You can bend and straighten your arm at the elbow until it is straight. Bending backwards is not possible; a bone stops the movement.
82986.m: The elbow only straightens the arm until it is straight.

82987.q: Which nerve causes the tingling when you knock your elbow?
82987.e: The ulnar nerve lies at the elbow directly under the skin. If it gets knocked, it tingles all the way into the little finger.
82987.m: The ulnar nerve tingles when you knock your elbow.

82988.q: What is injured in a sprain?
82988.e: In a sprain, the ligaments around a joint are overstretched. The bone is not broken.
82988.m: In a sprain, the ligaments are overstretched.

82989.q: How can you often recognise a sprain?
82989.e: After a sprain, the joint hurts and swells up. You often can hardly move it.

82990.q: What does the E stand for in the RICE rule for sports injuries?
82990.e: RICE stands for Rest, Ice, Compression and Elevation. Elevation means raising the injured part of the body above the heart so it swells less.

82991.q: What is the right way to put an ice pack on a sprained joint?
82991.e: Ice directly on the skin can damage the skin. A cloth in between protects the skin and still cools it.
82991.m: Wrap ice packs in a cloth.

82992.q: Should you carry on playing football with a freshly sprained foot?
82992.e: An injured joint needs rest, otherwise the injury gets worse. That is why you stop playing straight away.
82992.m: With a sprain, you stop playing straight away.

82993.q: Where do you most often get a sprain when running and jumping?
82993.e: When running and jumping, you easily go over on your foot. That is why the ankle is the joint most often sprained.
82993.m: The foot is the most commonly sprained.

82994.q: Why does the skin often turn blue with a sprain?
82994.e: In the injury, small blood vessels tear. The blood collects under the skin and forms a bruise.
82994.m: A bruise comes from blood under the skin.

82995.q: What helps to prevent sprains in sport?
a: Sitting still for a long time
82995.e: Warmed-up muscles and ligaments are more elastic. They hold the joint better, and you get injured less often.
82995.m: People who warm up get injured less often.

82996.q: What usually causes the cracking sound when someone cracks their knuckles?
a: A gas bubble in the joint
82996.e: When you pull on the joint, a gas bubble suddenly forms in the fluid inside it. That makes the cracking sound.
82996.m: Knuckle cracking comes from a gas bubble in the joint.

82997.q: Why can you not crack the same finger again straight away?
a: The gas first has to dissolve again
The finger has gone to sleep
82997.e: After cracking, it takes about 20 minutes for the gas to dissolve back into the joint fluid. Only then can it crack again.
82997.m: A cracked joint needs a break before it cracks again.

82998.q: When should you see a doctor about a cracking joint?
a: When it cracks in the morning
82998.e: Cracking without pain is usually harmless. But if the joint hurts or swells up, a doctor should have a look.
82998.m: Only painful joint cracking needs to be checked.

82999.q: Apart from a gas bubble, what can cause a cracking sound in a joint?
a: A tendon snapping over a bone
82999.e: Sometimes a tendon slides over a bump on a bone when you move. This can also crack or snap.
82999.m: A snapping tendon can crack too.

83000.q: A doctor cracked the knuckles of only one hand for over 50 years. What did he find?
83000.e: The doctor Donald Unger cracked only the knuckles of his left hand and then compared both hands. Neither hand developed a joint disease, and in 2009 he received a joke prize for research.
83000.m: According to what we know today, knuckle cracking does not make joints ill.

83001.q: Where do many people hear a crack when they stand up from a deep squat?
83001.e: Many people’s knees crack when bending deeply and straightening. Without pain, this is usually harmless.
83001.m: Knees often crack when you stand up from a squat.

83002.q: Who is usually more flexible: children or older people?
83002.e: In children, muscles, tendons and ligaments are still very stretchy. With age, flexibility decreases if you do not practise it.
83002.m: Children are usually more flexible than older people.

83003.q: When should you stretch during sport?
a: Straight after getting up in bed
83003.e: Warm muscles stretch better. That is why you warm up first and only stretch afterwards.
83003.m: Only stretch when your muscles are warm.

83004.q: In which sport do you perform on the floor and on apparatus such as the high bar and parallel bars?
83004.e: Artistic gymnasts need a lot of strength and great flexibility. They show their routines on the floor and on different pieces of apparatus.
83004.m: Artistic gymnastics needs a lot of strength and flexibility.

83005.q: What is it better not to do when stretching?
83005.e: Jerky bouncing can injure muscles. It is better to move slowly into the stretch and hold it calmly.

83006.q: What is the gymnastics exercise called where you stand on your hands and feet, bent backwards?
83006.e: In the bridge, the body forms a high arch. This needs a very flexible back and flexible shoulders.
83006.m: You need a flexible back for the bridge.

83007.q: What are you testing when you sit with straight legs and reach for your toes?
83007.e: The further forwards you get, the more flexible your back and the muscles at the back of your legs are. This test is often done in PE.
83007.m: Reaching for your toes shows how flexible you are.

83008.q: In which kind of exercise are there poses such as ‘downward dog’?
83008.e: Yoga is made up of many poses with animal names. They stretch the body and make it flexible.

83009.q: What do you call circus performers who can bend their bodies extremely?
83009.e: Contortionists are so flexible that they can bend almost like a snake. They practise for years to do it.

83010.q: What happens to your flexibility if you move very little for a long time?
83010.e: If muscles and joints are moved very little, they become stiffer. Regular exercise keeps you flexible.
83010.m: If you move little, you get stiffer.

83011.q: Which sea creature has no bones and can squeeze through tiny gaps?
83011.e: An octopus has no skeleton made of bones. Only its hard beak does not fit through every opening; the rest is completely soft.
83011.m: An octopus can squeeze through the tiniest gaps.

83012.q: What do you do with your chin before you do a forward roll?
83012.e: With your chin on your chest, your neck becomes rounded. That way you roll over your back instead of your head.
83012.m: In a forward roll, tuck your chin to your chest.

83013.q: What should your back be like in a forward roll?
83013.e: A round back rolls softly over the mat. A straight back would thump hard onto the floor.
83013.m: In a forward roll, make your back round.

83014.q: Where do you put your hands in a forward roll?
a: Shoulder-width apart in front of your feet
83014.e: Your hands are on the mat in front of your feet, shoulder-width apart. They brake and help you roll.
83014.m: In a forward roll, your hands are in front of your feet.

83015.q: What is the somersault forwards called in PE?
83015.e: In gymnastics, the somersault is called a forward roll. You roll forwards over your rounded back.
83015.m: In gymnastics, the somersault is called a forward roll.

83016.q: What is the gymnastics exercise called where you roll backwards over your back?
83016.e: In a backward roll, you roll backwards from a crouch. Your hands push off the floor next to your ears.
83016.m: To roll backwards, you do a backward roll.

83017.q: What do you practise forward rolls on in PE?
83017.e: A mat is soft and cushions you. That way rolling does not hurt.
83017.m: You practise forward rolls on a mat.

83018.q: What helps beginners learn a forward roll?
83018.e: On a sloping surface you roll forwards more easily by yourself. That makes the movement easier to learn.
83018.m: A sloping mat makes the forward roll easier.

83019.q: What is a flip in the air called, where your hands do not touch the ground?
83019.e: In a somersault, you turn all the way round once in the air. You land on your feet again.
83019.m: A somersault is a flip in the air.

83020.q: What do you do in the splits?
a: Spread your legs wide apart in a line
83020.e: In the splits, you sit on the floor with straight legs. The legs point in opposite directions and form a straight line.
83020.m: In the splits, your legs form a straight line.

83021.q: What are the splits called where one leg points forwards and the other backwards?
83021.e: The legs lie lengthways in the direction you are facing. That is why they are called front splits.
83021.m: In the front splits, one leg points forwards and the other backwards.

83022.q: What are the splits called where both legs point to the side?
83022.e: The legs are spread out to the left and right. This form is called the side splits and is especially hard for many people.
83022.m: In the side splits, both legs point to the side.

83023.q: In which dance do dancers often show the splits?
83023.e: Ballet needs a lot of flexibility. Splits and jumps with the legs spread wide are part of it.
83023.m: The splits are often part of ballet.

83024.q: What is the safest way to learn the splits?
83024.e: Muscles and tendons only become more stretchy slowly. If you practise a little every day, you make safe progress without injury.
83024.m: You learn the splits with patience and regular stretching.

83025.q: Which muscles are stretched when you spread your legs to the side?
a: The muscles on the inside of the thigh
The muscles on the upper arm
83025.e: When spreading your legs sideways, the muscles on the inside of the thighs pull. They have to give way so the legs can go wide apart.
83025.m: Spreading your legs stretches the inner thighs.

83026.q: Which joints have to be especially mobile for the splits?
83026.e: In the splits, the legs are spread wide at the hip joint. The more mobile the hip is, the lower you can get.
83026.m: For the splits you need mobile hips.

83028.q: What should you do if you suddenly feel a stabbing pain while practising the splits?
83028.e: A stabbing pain can mean that a muscle is injured. Then you stop straight away and take a break.
83028.m: If it stabs, stop straight away.

83029.q: What touches the ground one after another when you do a cartwheel?
83029.e: In a cartwheel, you first put down one hand and then the other. Then both feet land one after the other.
83029.m: In a cartwheel, first the hands come down and then the feet.

83030.q: What are your legs like in the air during a cartwheel?
83030.e: The straight, spread legs turn over your head. That is why a cartwheel looks like a star.
83030.m: In a cartwheel, your legs are straight and spread.

83031.q: In which direction do you move when doing a cartwheel?
a: Round in a circle on the spot
83031.e: In a cartwheel, you turn sideways over your hands. You land on the same line, but a bit further along.

83032.q: Why is the gymnastics move called a ‘cartwheel’?
a: Arms and legs turn like spokes
You need a bike for it
83032.e: Your arms and legs are stretched out wide and turn around the middle of your body. This is like the spokes of a wheel.
83032.m: In a cartwheel, arms and legs turn like spokes.

83033.q: What is a cartwheel with a quarter turn called, where you land on both feet at the same time?
83033.e: In a round-off, you turn at the end and land with your legs together. You then face the direction you came from.
83033.m: In a round-off, you land on both feet at the same time.

83034.q: Which parts of the body briefly carry your whole weight when doing a cartwheel?
83034.e: When your legs are in the air, you are supported only on your hands. That is why you need strength in your arms and shoulders.
83034.m: In a cartwheel, your arms briefly carry your whole body.

83035.q: What helps when practising so that your cartwheel is nice and straight?
83035.e: Your hands and feet should land on the same straight line. A line on the floor helps you keep the direction.
83035.m: A line on the floor helps with a straight cartwheel.

83036.q: Where are your arms when you take a run-up for a cartwheel?
a: Folded in front of your tummy
83036.e: At the start you stretch your arms up high. That way you can swing forwards onto your hands.
83036.m: For a cartwheel, first stretch your arms up high.

83037.q: How can you make a cartwheel harder once you are good at it?
83037.e: If you can do a cartwheel safely, you practise it with only one hand on the floor. This needs even more strength and balance.

83231.q: What is melted rock called while it is still deep inside the Earth?
83231.e: Under the ground, melted rock is called magma. Only at the surface is it called lava.
83231.m: Under the ground, liquid rock is called magma.

83232.q: What colour is fresh, very hot lava?
83232.e: Very hot lava glows like the embers in a fireplace. That is why it shines red to orange.
83232.m: Fresh lava glows red and orange.

83233.e: Lava is much hotter than boiling water at 100 degrees. Depending on the type, it is about 700 to 1200 degrees.
83233.m: Lava is much hotter than boiling water.

83234.q: What does lava turn into when it cools down?
83234.e: When lava cools down, it becomes solid. This makes new rock, for example dark basalt.

83235.q: What happens when a lava flow runs into the sea?
83235.e: The seawater instantly turns to steam on the hot lava. Big clouds of steam rise up.
83235.m: Lava in the sea makes the water hiss and steam.

83236.q: How fast does a lava flow often move?
a: As fast as a racing car
83236.e: Many lava flows move slowly down the mountain. But they can still destroy houses.

83237.q: On which islands in the Pacific can you often see lava flows?
83237.e: Hawaii is made of volcanoes that often pour out runny lava. It flows in long streams all the way to the sea.
83237.m: There are often lava flows on Hawaii.

a: A lump of lava flying through the air
A firework on Swiss National Day
83238.e: During an eruption, the volcano hurls scraps of lava into the air. They fall back down as volcanic bombs.
83238.m: A volcanic bomb is a flying lump of lava.

83239.q: What happens to a volcanic bomb while it is flying through the air?
a: It cools down and becomes solid
83239.e: In the air, the outside of the lump of lava cools down. That is why the bomb is already fairly solid when it lands.
83239.m: Volcanic bombs become solid in flight.

83240.q: What shape are many volcanic bombs?
83240.e: The lump of lava spins as it flies. That is why it often becomes round, or pointed at both ends like a spindle.
83240.m: Many volcanic bombs are round or spindle-shaped.

83241.q: Why must you not go near the crater during an eruption?
a: Because it is too dark there
83241.e: Volcanic bombs can be heavy and very hot. Anyone who is hit can be badly hurt.
83241.m: During an eruption it is dangerous near the crater.

83242.q: How big can volcanic bombs get?
a: Some are as big as a car
Always as small as a grain of sand
Always as big as a house
83242.e: Many volcanic bombs are the size of a fist. But there are also huge chunks as big as a car.
83242.m: Volcanic bombs can be very big.

83243.q: What are the little stones called that a volcano throws out, which are smaller than bombs?
83243.e: Lapilli is Italian and means little stones. They are about the size of peas up to nuts.
83243.m: Little stones from a volcano are called lapilli.

83244.q: How hot is a volcanic bomb when it flies out of the volcano?
a: Cool like a stone in the forest
83244.e: A volcanic bomb is a lump of lava. When it flies out of the volcano, it is red hot.

83245.q: What do you often hear when a volcano throws out bombs?
83245.e: During the eruption, big gas bubbles burst in the lava. This makes loud bangs and hurls the lava upwards.
83245.m: When volcanic bombs are thrown out, there are loud bangs.

83246.q: What shape is a volcanic crater usually?
83246.e: A crater is a round hollow. It looks like a big bowl.
83246.m: A volcanic crater looks like a bowl.

83247.q: What can form in an extinct volcanic crater?
83247.e: Rainwater collects in the crater when the volcano is no longer active. This makes a crater lake.
83247.m: A lake can form in an old crater.

83248.q: What often rises from the crater of an active volcano?
83248.e: Even without a big eruption, gases and steam come out of the crater. That is why you often see a cloud above it.
83248.m: Gases often rise from the crater.

83249.q: What is a huge, collapsed volcanic crater called?
83249.e: After a massive eruption, the volcano can collapse in on itself. This makes a huge basin, the caldera.
83249.m: A caldera is a huge collapsed crater.

83250.q: What are the small crater lakes in the Eifel in Germany called?
83250.e: There used to be volcanic eruptions in the Eifel. Today there are lakes in the round craters, which are called maars.
83250.m: The crater lakes in the Eifel are called maars.

83251.q: Does a volcano always have just one crater?
83251.e: Besides the main crater, many volcanoes have other craters on their sides. Lava can come out there too.
83251.m: A volcano can have several craters.

83252.q: What is volcanic ash made of?
83252.e: Volcanic ash is different from the ash in a fireplace. It is made of tiny bits of rock and glass.
83252.m: Volcanic ash is made of tiny bits of rock.

83253.q: Why is volcanic ash dangerous for aeroplanes?
83253.e: In the hot engines the ash melts and clogs them. That is why aeroplanes do not fly through ash clouds.
83253.m: Aeroplanes avoid clouds of volcanic ash.

83254.q: Which country did the ash cloud come from in 2010 that kept many aeroplanes on the ground in Europe?
83254.e: The volcano Eyjafjallajökull in Iceland erupted in 2010. Its ash travelled as far as central Europe, including Switzerland.
83254.m: In 2010, ash from Iceland stopped many flights in Europe.

83255.q: Which ancient Roman town was buried by volcanic ash in the year 79?
83255.e: Vesuvius in Italy erupted and covered Pompeii with ash. Today you can visit the excavated town.
83255.m: Pompeii was buried by volcanic ash.

83256.q: What should you wear when there is a lot of volcanic ash in the air?
83256.e: The fine grains of ash irritate the lungs. A mask helps you not to breathe them in.
83256.m: When there is volcanic ash in the air, a mask protects you.

83257.q: How far can the wind carry volcanic ash?
a: Only to the foot of the volcano
83257.e: Fine ash rises high into the sky. The wind can carry it thousands of kilometres.
83257.m: The wind carries volcanic ash very far.

83258.q: What colour is volcanic ash usually?
83258.e: Volcanic ash is usually grey to dark grey. It can cover cars, roads and roofs like grey snow.

83259.q: What shoots into the air at a geyser?
83259.e: Under a geyser, water is heated by hot rock. Then it shoots up as a hot fountain with steam.
83259.m: A geyser shoots hot water into the air.

83260.q: What does the Icelandic word “geysa”, which gives the geyser its name, mean?
83260.e: The Icelandic word geysa means to gush out violently. That is exactly what the hot water of a geyser does.
83260.m: The name geyser means something that gushes out violently.

83261.q: Which country in the north has lots of geysers?
83261.e: Iceland has many volcanoes and hot rock under the ground. That is why lots of geysers spout there.
83261.m: There are lots of geysers in Iceland.

83262.q: Where does the hot water of a geyser come from?
83262.e: Rainwater soaks deep into the ground. There it is heated by hot rock and shoots back up.
83262.m: The water of a geyser is heated deep inside the Earth.

83263.q: Why should you not go too close to a geyser?
83263.e: The water of a geyser can be almost boiling hot. You could scald yourself badly.

83264.q: Are there natural geysers in Switzerland?
83264.e: Geysers need hot rock close to the surface, as in Iceland. Switzerland does not have that.
83264.m: There are no natural geysers in Switzerland.

83265.q: What can you often see above a geyser, even when it is not spouting?
83265.e: The hot water in the pool is always steaming. On cold days especially, you see a lot of steam.
83265.m: Steam often rises above a geyser.

83266.q: What is special about pumice in water?
83266.e: Pumice is full of tiny air holes. That makes it so light that it floats on water.

a: It has lots of tiny holes
It is hollow inside like a balloon
83267.e: During an eruption, gas bubbles make the lava foam up. When it cools, the bubbles stay behind as holes in the stone.
83267.m: Pumice is full of tiny holes.

83268.q: What do many people use pumice for in the bathroom?
a: To rub hard skin off their feet
83268.e: Pumice is rough like sandpaper. You use it to gently rub hard skin off your feet.
83268.m: You rub hard skin off with pumice.

83269.q: What else is pumice used for?
83269.e: Because pumice is so light, it is used to make lightweight building blocks and mortar.
83269.m: Lightweight building blocks are made from pumice.

83270.e: Pumice is usually light coloured. It is often light grey, white or beige.

83271.e: Because of the many holes, the surface has sharp little edges. That is why it feels rough.

83272.q: What can float on the water after a volcanic eruption in the sea?
83272.e: Pumice is full of air holes and therefore light. After some underwater eruptions, huge rafts of pumice drift on the sea.
83272.m: After eruptions in the sea, pumice can drift on the water.

83273.q: What are some jeans washed with to make them look faded?
83273.e: The jeans were washed in the machine together with pumice stones. The rough stones rubbed off the colour.

83274.q: Which country does Mount Etna belong to?
83274.e: The island Etna stands on belongs to Italy. Italy is one of Switzerland's neighbouring countries.

83275.e: Etna is a volcano on Sicily. It is the highest active volcano in Europe.

a: Never any more, it is extinct
83276.e: Etna often has smaller and bigger eruptions. That is why scientists watch it all the time.

83277.q: What often lies on the summit of Etna in winter?
83277.e: Etna is so high that it snows at the top in winter. You can even go skiing there.
83277.m: There is often snow on Etna in winter.

83278.q: Which nuts grow especially well on Etna around Bronte?
83278.e: The little town of Bronte lies on the western slope of Etna. Famous green pistachios grow there.

83279.q: Which big city lies at the foot of Etna?
83279.e: Catania lies by the sea at the foot of Etna. In the past, lava has even flowed into the city.
83279.m: Catania lies at the foot of Etna.

83280.q: Why do many people live on Etna even though it often erupts?
a: The soil is good for fruit and vegetables
83280.e: Over time, old lava and ash turn into very fertile soil. That is why lots of fruit, vegetables and grapes for wine grow on Etna.

83281.q: Which word comes from the name of the island of Vulcano?
83281.e: The island of Vulcano gave its name to all fire-breathing mountains. That is why today we say volcano.
83281.m: The word volcano comes from the island of Vulcano.

83282.q: Which country does the island of Vulcano belong to?
83282.e: Vulcano lies in the Mediterranean north of Sicily. The island belongs to Italy.
83282.m: The island of Vulcano belongs to Italy.

83283.q: Which Roman god is the island of Vulcano named after?
83283.e: Vulcan was the Roman god of fire and blacksmiths. The Romans believed his workshop was under the island.
