83283.m: Vulcan was the Roman god of fire.

83284.q: Which sea is the island of Vulcano in?
83284.e: Vulcano lies in the Mediterranean north of Sicily. The island belongs to Italy.

83285.q: What do many visitors bathe in on the island of Vulcano?
83285.e: On Vulcano there is a pool of warm mud from the volcano. Lots of people bathe in it.
83285.m: On Vulcano you can bathe in warm mud.

83286.q: What does it smell of in many places on the island of Vulcano?
83286.e: Sulphur gases rise from the ground. They smell rather unpleasantly of rotten eggs.
83286.m: On Vulcano it smells of sulphur.

83287.q: When was the last big eruption on Vulcano?
83287.e: The last eruption lasted from 1888 to 1890. Since then the volcano has been quiet, but it is closely watched.
83287.m: The volcano on Vulcano has been quiet for over 100 years.

83288.q: How do you get to the island of Vulcano?
83288.e: Vulcano is an island with no bridge to the mainland. Ferries go across from Sicily.
83288.m: You get to Vulcano by boat.

83289.e: Stromboli is a small island in the Mediterranean. It is made of an active volcano.

83290.q: Because of its many small eruptions, what else is Stromboli called?
83290.e: Stromboli often spits out glowing lava at night. Sailors saw it from far away like a light.
83290.m: Stromboli is also called the Lighthouse of the Mediterranean.

83291.q: How often does Stromboli have small eruptions?
a: Very often, usually several times an hour
Never any more, it is extinct
83291.e: Stromboli has been active almost all the time for a very long time. There are usually small eruptions several times an hour.
83291.m: Stromboli erupts a little very often.

83292.q: Do people live on the island of Stromboli?
83292.e: On Stromboli there are small villages by the sea. A few hundred people live there.
83292.m: People live on the volcanic island of Stromboli.

83293.q: Where does the glowing lava on the island of Stromboli usually slide?
83293.e: On one side of Stromboli there is a steep slope. There the lava rolls down into the sea, far away from the villages.
83293.m: On Stromboli, the lava slides into the sea.

83294.q: Roughly how high does Stromboli rise above the sea?
83294.e: The summit of Stromboli is about 920 metres above the sea. But most of the volcano is under water.

83295.q: When can you see Stromboli's glowing eruptions best?
83295.e: In the dark, the glowing lava shines brightly. During the day you mostly see smoke.
83295.m: Stromboli glows most beautifully at night.

83296.q: Which volcano gives its name to a type of eruption with small, regular explosions?
83296.e: Small, regular eruptions in which scraps of lava fly up are called Strombolian. They are named after Stromboli.
83296.m: Strombolian eruptions are named after Stromboli.

83297.q: Where should you go first at school during an earthquake?
83297.e: Under a sturdy table you are protected from things falling down. You practise this in an earthquake drill.
83297.m: In an earthquake, get under the table.

83298.q: What should you do under the table during an earthquake?
a: Protect your head and hold on
Cover your eyes and go to sleep
83298.e: You protect your head with one arm and hold on to the table leg with the other hand. That way the table does not slide away.
83298.m: Under the table, protect your head and hold on.

83299.q: What should you stay away from during an earthquake?
83299.e: Window panes can break during the quake. The splinters of glass are dangerous.
83299.m: In an earthquake, stay away from windows.

83300.q: What should you not use when leaving the building after an earthquake?
83300.e: The lift can get stuck because of a power cut. That is why you go out calmly by the stairs.
83300.m: After an earthquake, use the stairs, not the lift.

83301.q: Where are you safest outdoors during an earthquake?
a: Right next to a house wall
83301.e: In an open space nothing can fall on you. Walls, trees and power lines can fall over.
83301.m: Outdoors, an open space is safest during an earthquake.

83302.q: Why do you practise at school what to do in an earthquake?
a: So you do the right thing in an emergency
So you learn to count tables
83302.e: In a real earthquake you get a fright. If you have practised beforehand, you know straight away what to do.
83302.m: If you practise, you know what to do in an emergency.

83303.q: What should you do if you are in bed during an earthquake?
a: Stay lying down and protect your head with the pillow
83303.e: Walking around in the dark is dangerous. In bed, the pillow protects your head from things falling down.
83303.m: In bed during a quake, protect your head with the pillow.

83304.q: In which country do schoolchildren practise for earthquakes especially often?
83304.e: Japan has a great many earthquakes. That is why all children there regularly practise how to protect themselves.
83304.m: In Japan, children often practise for earthquakes.

83305.q: What should you do at the assembly point outside after an earthquake?
a: Go back into the school building
Look for a hiding place on your own
83305.e: At the assembly point the teacher counts whether all the children are there. That way you know nobody is missing.
83305.m: At the assembly point, wait until everyone is there.

83306.e: A seismograph senses how strongly the ground is shaking. That way earthquakes can be measured.

83307.q: What does a seismograph draw during an earthquake?
83307.e: When the ground is calm, the line is almost straight. During an earthquake it swings strongly back and forth.
83307.m: During a quake, a seismograph draws a zigzag line.

83308.q: What do you feel during an earthquake?
83308.e: In an earthquake the Earth moves. You feel the ground trembling and shaking.
83308.m: In an earthquake the ground shakes.

83309.q: What does a very big spike on a seismogram mean?
83309.e: The more strongly the ground shakes, the bigger the swings. So big spikes show a strong quake.
83309.m: Big spikes mean a strong earthquake.

83310.q: Which organisation in Switzerland watches earthquakes with lots of seismographs?
83310.e: The Swiss Seismological Service is part of ETH Zurich. It has set up measuring instruments all over the country.
83310.m: The Swiss Seismological Service measures earthquakes in Switzerland.

83311.q: Can seismographs also measure earthquakes that you cannot feel yourself?
83311.e: Seismographs are very sensitive. They also measure very weak earthquakes that nobody notices.
83311.m: Seismographs sense even very weak earthquakes.

83312.q: In which country was an earthquake detector with dragons built almost 2000 years ago?
83312.e: In the year 132, the scholar Zhang Heng built a device with dragons' heads. During a quake, a ball fell into the mouth of a toad.
83312.m: An earthquake detector was built in China long ago.

83313.q: Roughly how many earthquakes are measured in Switzerland each year?
83313.e: The Swiss Seismological Service measures around 1000 to 1500 earthquakes every year. Most of them are so weak that you cannot feel them.
83313.m: There are lots of small earthquakes in Switzerland every year.

83314.q: What heats up the water of a hot spring?
a: The heat deep inside the Earth
83314.e: The deeper you go into the Earth, the warmer it gets. The water flows through warm rock deep down and comes back up warm.
83314.m: The Earth's heat warms hot springs.

83315.q: In which town in the canton of Aargau did the Romans already bathe in warm spring water?
83315.e: The town of Baden has hot springs that the Romans already knew. The town's name means “baths” in German.
83315.m: The Romans already bathed in warm water in Baden.

83316.q: Which place in Valais is known for its many hot springs?
83316.e: In Leukerbad, lots of hot springs bubble out of the ground. There are big thermal baths there.
83316.m: Leukerbad in Valais has many hot springs.

83317.q: Which animals in Japan like to bathe in hot springs in winter?
83317.e: Snow monkeys live in the mountains of Japan. In winter they warm up in hot springs.
83317.m: In Japan, monkeys bathe in hot springs.

83318.q: What is a bath with warm water from the earth called?
83318.e: Thermal means warm. In a thermal bath you bathe in naturally warm spring water.
83318.m: In a thermal bath you bathe in warm spring water.

83319.q: Why do many people like bathing outdoors at a thermal bath even in winter?
83319.e: In a thermal bath, warm water comes out of the earth. That is why you can bathe outdoors in warm water even when it snows.
83319.m: In a thermal bath the water is warm even in winter.

83320.q: What is often dissolved in the water of hot springs?
83320.e: The water flows through the rock for a long time. On the way it dissolves minerals such as lime or sulphur.
83320.m: Hot spring water often contains minerals.

83321.q: Why do hot springs steam especially strongly in winter?
83321.e: The warm water gives off vapour. In cold air you can see this vapour especially well as mist.
83321.m: In cold air you can see the steam of hot springs well.

83322.q: What do volcanologists wear when they go close to a lava flow?
83322.e: A lava flow gives off great heat. A silvery suit reflects the heat and protects the scientists.
83322.m: Volcanologists protect themselves with a heat protection suit.

83323.q: What happens to trees that a lava flow reaches?
83323.e: Lava is so hot that wood catches fire at once. That is why trees in the path of a lava flow burn down.

83324.q: What can lie deep down in the crater of an active volcano?
83324.e: In some volcanoes, the lava sits in the crater like in a pot. This is called a lava lake.
83324.m: There can be a lake of lava in the crater.

83325.q: Why do people not climb down into the crater of an active volcano?
a: Because of poisonous gases and heat
Because it is too cold there
Because the path is too short
83325.e: Poisonous gases collect in the crater, and an eruption can suddenly happen. That is extremely dangerous.
83325.m: It is dangerous in the crater of an active volcano.

83326.e: Etna is over 3000 metres high. Its height changes a little because new rock is added during eruptions.

83327.q: What happens at a geyser between two eruptions?
a: It fills up with water again
83327.e: After the eruption, water flows back into the vent and is heated again. When it is hot enough, the geyser spouts again.
83327.m: A geyser fills up again between eruptions.

83328.q: What is a hot spring for bathing called in Japan?
83328.e: There are thousands of hot springs in Japan. A bath in one is called an onsen and is very popular.
83328.m: A hot spring in Japan is called an onsen.

83329.q: What happens to the sky when there is a lot of volcanic ash in the air?
83329.e: A thick ash cloud blocks the sunlight. Then it can get almost dark in the middle of the day.
83329.m: Lots of volcanic ash makes the sky dark.

83330.q: What is a candle usually made of?
83330.e: Candles are usually made of wax. The wax is the candle's fuel.
83330.m: A candle is usually made of wax.

83331.q: What material is a candle's wick usually made of?
83331.e: The wick is usually made of plaited cotton threads. They soak up the liquid wax well.
83331.m: A candle wick is usually made of cotton.

83332.q: What happens to the wax close to a candle's flame?
83332.e: The heat of the flame melts the wax. The liquid wax rises up the wick and burns there.
83332.m: The heat of the flame makes the wax liquid.

83333.q: Which animals provide wax for candles?
83333.e: Bees build their honeycombs from wax. Candles can be made from this beeswax.

83334.q: Why should you never put a candle right next to a curtain?
83334.e: Fabric burns easily. If the curtain moves towards the flame, a fire can start.
83334.m: Candles need to be kept away from anything that can burn.

83335.q: What do you do with a burning candle before leaving the room?
a: You put it by the window
83335.e: A candle must never burn without someone watching. Anyone who goes out blows it out first.
83335.m: Never leave a burning candle alone.

83336.q: What is the best thing to stand a candle on?
83336.e: A sturdy candle holder does not burn and does not tip over so easily. Cushions, paper and blankets can catch fire.
83336.m: A candle belongs on a sturdy holder that does not burn.

83337.q: What colour is the bottom part of a candle flame?
83337.e: Right at the bottom, the flame gets a lot of air and burns bluish. Further up it glows yellow.
83337.m: At the bottom, a candle flame is blue.

83338.q: Which way does a candle flame point?
83338.e: Hot air is lighter than cold air and rises. That is why the flame points upwards.
83338.m: A flame points upwards because hot air rises.

83340.q: Which gas from the air does a flame need?
83340.e: Fire needs oxygen to burn. Oxygen is part of the air.
83340.m: A flame needs oxygen from the air.

83341.q: What is the picture of the three things a fire needs called?
83341.e: Fire needs something that burns, air and enough heat. If one of them is missing, the fire goes out.
83341.m: The fire triangle shows what a fire needs to burn.

83342.q: What is a tiny glowing bit that jumps out of a fire called?
83342.e: Glowing bits can fly out of a fire. Sparks like these can set other things alight.
83342.m: A spark is a tiny glowing bit.

83343.q: What do you call a big fire that has got out of control?
83343.e: A blaze is a fire that spreads when nobody wants it to. It can destroy houses and forests.
83343.m: A fire out of control is called a blaze.

83344.q: What usually happens if you blow hard on a candle flame?
83344.e: The puff of air blows the hot gases away and cools the flame. Then it goes out.
83344.m: Blowing hard puts out a candle flame.

83345.e: A campfire is made outside at a safe fireplace. You can sit by it and roast sausages.
83345.m: A campfire burns outdoors at a fireplace.

83347.q: What is the stick of a match usually made of?
83347.e: The stick is a thin piece of wood. It burns once the head has caught fire.
83347.m: A match usually has a wooden stick.

83348.q: What is the thick part at the end of a match called?
83348.e: At the end is the match head. It contains substances that catch fire when rubbed.
83348.m: The head of a match catches fire when rubbed.

83349.q: Where does a safety match light?
a: On the striking surface of the box
83349.e: Safety matches only light when you strike them on the striking surface of the box. That is why they are called safety matches.
83349.m: A safety match lights on the striking surface of the box.

83350.q: Which substance is in the striking surface of a matchbox?
83350.e: The striking surface contains red phosphorus. Striking produces so much heat that the match head catches fire.
83350.m: The striking surface contains red phosphorus.

83351.q: In which country was the safety match invented?
83351.e: The safety match was invented in Sweden around 1844. That is why they are sometimes called Swedish matches.
83351.m: The safety match comes from Sweden.

83352.q: When may small children use matches?
83352.e: Accidents happen quickly with fire. That is why children only practise lighting matches together with adults.
83352.m: Children only light matches with adults.

83353.q: Apart from a match, what can you use to light a candle?
83353.e: A lighter makes a small flame. A torch only makes light, not fire.
83353.m: A lighter can also light a candle.

83354.q: What do you often smell first when something is burning somewhere?
83354.e: When something burns, it makes smoke with a sharp smell. You often smell it before you see the fire.
83354.m: A burning smell can be the first sign of a fire.

83355.q: Why should you crawl along the floor in a smoke-filled room?
a: There is less smoke down low
83355.e: In a fire, the air near the floor stays clean for longer. There you can breathe and see better.
83355.m: In smoke, crawl along the floor because the air is better there.

83356.q: What is often the most dangerous thing in a fire in a flat?
83356.e: Smoke is poisonous and spreads very fast. Just a few breaths can make you pass out.
83356.m: Smoke from a fire is very dangerous because it is poisonous.

83357.e: Smoke contains hot gases and very fine particles. The particles make the smoke visible.
83357.m: Smoke is made of gases and tiny particles.

83358.q: What does smoke coming from a chimney on the roof show?
a: A fire is burning in the stove
It is raining in the house
83358.e: When wood burns in the stove, the smoke goes out through the chimney. That is why you see it on the roof.
83358.m: Smoke from the chimney shows that a fire is burning in the stove.

83359.q: What does smoke often do to your eyes?
83359.e: The particles and gases in smoke irritate the eyes. That is why they sting and water.

83360.q: Complete the saying: ‘There's no smoke without ...’
83360.e: Smoke almost always comes from a fire. The saying means that every rumour has a reason behind it.
83360.m: Where there is smoke, there is usually fire.

83361.q: What do you do if there is smoke in the stairwell while you are in the flat?
a: Keep the door shut and call for help
83361.e: You can suffocate in a smoke-filled stairwell. The closed door keeps the smoke out until the fire brigade arrives.
83361.m: If there is smoke in the stairwell, stay behind the closed door.

83362.q: What rises above a sooty candle?
a: A thin black thread of smoke
83362.e: If a candle burns unsteadily, for example because the wick is too long, soot rises as a dark thread. Then you trim the wick.
83362.m: A sooty candle often has a wick that is too long.

83363.q: What is soot mainly made of?
83363.e: Soot is mainly made of tiny particles of carbon. They are left over when something does not burn completely.

83364.q: When is a lot of soot produced?
a: When something burns with too little air
83364.e: If there is not enough air, the fuel does not burn completely. Then black particles are left over.
83364.m: Too little air produces a lot of soot.

83365.q: Why does a candle flame glow yellow?
83365.e: Tiny soot particles form in the flame. They get very hot and glow yellow.
83365.m: Glowing soot particles make the candle flame yellow.

83366.q: What appears if you hold a cold spoon in a candle flame for a moment?
83366.e: The flame cools down on the cold spoon. The soot settles as a black spot.
83366.m: A cold spoon in the flame turns black from soot.

83367.q: Who cleans the soot out of chimneys?
83367.e: The chimney sweep cleans chimneys and stoves. That way the soot cannot catch fire and the smoke can escape properly.
83367.m: The chimney sweep cleans the soot out of the chimney.

83368.q: Which job is thought to bring good luck?
83368.e: In the past, the chimney sweep protected houses from fires. That is why chimney sweeps are still thought to bring good luck today.
83368.m: The chimney sweep is thought to bring good luck.

83369.q: What was black ink for writing made from in the past?
83369.e: Soot was mixed with water and glue. This made black ink for writing and painting.
83369.m: Black ink used to be made from soot.

83370.q: Where does wood ash go once it has cooled down completely?
83370.e: Completely cold ash with no embers may go in the rubbish. It does not belong in the recycling collections.
83370.m: Cooled ash belongs in the rubbish.

83371.q: What colour is wood ash usually?
83371.e: Wood ash is usually light grey to grey. It is a soft powder.

83372.q: Why should ash not be emptied into the rubbish bag straight away?
a: There may still be embers in it
83372.e: Embers can stay hidden in ash for a long time. In the rubbish bag they could start a fire.
83372.m: Embers can stay hidden in ash for a long time.

83373.q: What is the safest thing to keep fresh ash in?
a: A metal bucket with a lid
83373.e: Metal does not burn. The lid keeps air away, so leftover embers cannot set anything alight.
83373.m: Fresh ash goes in a metal bucket with a lid.

83374.q: How heavy is the ash compared with the wood before?
83374.e: When it burns, almost all of the wood turns into gases. Only a small amount is left behind as ash.
83374.m: Ash is much lighter than the wood was.

83375.q: What did people make from wood ash and fat in the past?
83375.e: An alkali was made from wood ash and water. Boiled with fat, it turned into soap.
83375.m: In the past, soap was made from ash and fat.

83376.q: What do some gardeners use wood ash for?
83376.e: Wood ash contains substances that plants need. That is why some people sprinkle small amounts of it in the garden.
83376.m: Wood ash can be a fertiliser for plants.

83377.q: What are the still glowing remains of a fire called?
83377.e: Embers glow red and are very hot, even without a flame. Never touch them.
83377.m: Embers are the glowing remains of a fire.

83378.q: What colour are fire extinguishers usually?
83378.e: Fire extinguishers are usually red. That way you can find them quickly in an emergency.

83379.q: What is a fire extinguisher for?
83379.e: With a fire extinguisher you can fight a small fire. Big fires are put out by the fire brigade.
83379.m: A fire extinguisher puts out small fires.

83380.q: What pushes the extinguishing agent out of a fire extinguisher?
83380.e: Inside the fire extinguisher is a gas under pressure. When you squeeze the handle, it forces the extinguishing agent through the hose.
83380.m: A gas under pressure drives the agent out of the fire extinguisher.

83381.q: What comes out of a foam extinguisher?
83381.e: A foam extinguisher sprays foam. The foam covers what is burning and cools it.
83381.m: A foam extinguisher puts out fires with foam.

83382.q: What do you have to pull out before a fire extinguisher will work?
83382.e: A pin locks the handle. Only when it has been pulled out can you put out the fire.
83382.m: With a fire extinguisher, you first pull out the safety pin.

83383.q: Where do you aim the jet of a fire extinguisher?
a: At the base of the burning object
Into the air above the fire
83383.e: You put out the fire where it is really burning, at the bottom where it starts. Spraying into the smoke does little good.
83383.m: Aim at the bottom of the burning object, not into the smoke.

83384.q: Where is a fire extinguisher usually kept in a school building?
a: On the wall where it is easy to see
83384.e: In an emergency you have to find the fire extinguisher quickly. That is why it hangs where it is easy to see in the corridor, often with a sign.
83384.m: Fire extinguishers hang on the wall where they are easy to see.

83385.q: Who should use a fire extinguisher?
83385.e: A fire extinguisher is heavy and must be used properly. Children fetch help and get themselves to safety.
83385.m: Fire extinguishers are used by adults.

83386.q: About how long can a small fire extinguisher spray for?
83386.e: A small hand-held fire extinguisher is often empty after only about 10 to 20 seconds. That is why you have to aim carefully.
83386.m: A small fire extinguisher is empty after just a few seconds.

83387.q: What is a fire blanket for?
83387.e: You cover a small fire with a fire blanket. This smothers it.
83387.m: A fire blanket smothers small fires.

83388.q: How does a fire blanket put out a fire?
a: It takes the air away from the fire
83388.e: Under the blanket no fresh air can reach the fire. Without air it goes out.
83388.m: The fire blanket takes away the fire's air.

83389.q: In which room is a fire blanket often kept?
83389.e: The kitchen is where cooking and frying happen. Oil in a pan can easily catch fire there.
83389.m: A fire blanket often hangs in the kitchen.

83390.q: What can you cover a burning pan with if there is no fire blanket?
83390.e: A metal lid does not burn and closes the pan tightly. Without air, the fire goes out.
83390.m: A lid that fits can put out a burning pan.

83391.q: What is a fire blanket often made of?
83391.e: Fire blankets are made of a fabric that does not burn, often glass fibre. Paper, plastic and silk would catch fire.
83391.m: A fire blanket is made of a fabric that does not burn.

83392.q: How do you get a fire blanket out of its case quickly?
83392.e: Two tapes hang from the case. If you pull them hard, the blanket falls out.
83392.m: Pull the tapes to get the fire blanket out.

83393.q: Why do you hold the fire blanket so that your hands are behind it?
83393.e: The blanket is like a shield in front of the flames. That way you don't burn your hands.
83393.m: Behind the fire blanket, your hands are protected.

83394.q: What do you do with the fire blanket after covering the pan?
a: You pull it off at once
83394.e: It can stay hot under the blanket for a long time. If you lift it off too soon, the fire can flare up again.
83394.m: Leave the fire blanket in place until everything has cooled down.

83395.q: What does a smoke alarm do when it detects smoke?
83395.e: A smoke alarm makes a very loud warning sound. That way everyone is warned, even while asleep.
83395.m: A smoke alarm warns with a loud beep.

83396.q: Where is a smoke alarm fitted?
83396.e: The smoke alarm detects smoke where it gathers first in a room. That way it warns as early as possible.
83396.m: A smoke alarm belongs on the ceiling.

83397.q: What does a smoke alarm usually need in order to work?
83397.e: Most smoke alarms have a battery. That way they work even in a power cut.
83397.m: A smoke alarm usually needs a battery.

83398.q: How do you check whether a smoke alarm works?
83398.e: Every smoke alarm has a test button. When you press it, the warning sound must go off.
83398.m: You check a smoke alarm with the test button.

83399.q: Why is a smoke alarm in the bedroom especially important?
a: You can't smell smoke while asleep
Cooking is done in the bedroom
83399.e: Sleeping people do not notice smoke and do not wake up from it. The loud sound of the smoke alarm wakes them.
83399.m: A smoke alarm wakes us because we can't smell smoke while asleep.

83400.q: What do you do if the smoke alarm goes off and there is a fire?
83400.e: Smoke spreads very fast. That is why you go out at once and get help outside.
83400.m: When the smoke alarm goes off, leave the flat at once.

83401.q: What does a short beep from a smoke alarm every few minutes often mean?
a: There is a fire in the cellar
83401.e: Many smoke alarms give a short beep when the battery gets weak. Then it needs changing soon.
83401.m: A short beep often means a weak battery.

83402.q: How often should you check a smoke alarm?
a: Only when there is a fire
83402.e: Only a working smoke alarm can warn you. That is why you check it regularly with the test button.

83403.q: What shape are the hazard symbols on chemicals?
83403.e: The hazard symbols are diamonds, that is squares standing on one corner. Inside is a black picture.

83404.q: What colour is the border of a hazard symbol?
83404.e: Hazard symbols have a red border and a white background. The black picture shows the danger.
83404.m: Hazard symbols have a red border.

83405.q: What does the hazard symbol with a flame mean?
83405.e: The flame shows that this substance can catch fire easily. Keep it away from heat and flames.
83405.m: The flame symbol warns of highly flammable substances.

83406.q: What does the hazard symbol with a skull and crossbones mean?
83406.e: The skull and crossbones warns of very poisonous substances. Even small amounts can be deadly.
83406.m: The skull and crossbones warns of poison.

83407.q: What does the hazard symbol with a dead tree and a fish mean?
83407.e: This substance harms animals and plants, especially in water. It must not go down the drain.
83407.m: The tree and fish warn of danger to the environment.

83408.q: What does the hazard symbol with an exploding bomb mean?
83408.e: The exploding bomb warns of substances that can explode. You have to be very careful with them.
83408.m: The bomb warns of explosive substances.

83409.q: What does the hazard symbol with a flame over a circle mean?
83409.e: Such substances give off oxygen. They make a fire stronger, even if they do not burn themselves.
83409.m: The flame over a circle warns of oxidising substances.

83410.q: On which things at home do you often find hazard symbols?
83410.e: Many cleaning products contain dangerous substances. That is why they carry hazard symbols.
83410.m: Many cleaning products carry hazard symbols.

83411.q: What does the hazard symbol with drops attacking a hand mean?
83411.e: Corrosive substances can injure skin and eyes. That is why the symbol shows a hand being attacked.
83411.m: The symbol with the hand warns of corrosive substances.

83412.q: What is the first thing you do in a fire?
83412.e: The rule is: raise the alarm, rescue, put out. First you call for help, then you get people to safety.
83412.m: In a fire, first raise the alarm, then rescue, then put it out.

83413.q: What should you do if your own clothes are on fire?
83413.e: Running gives the fire more air. If you lie down and roll, you smother the flames.
83413.m: If your clothes are on fire, lie down and roll.

83414.q: What do you use to get out of a building on fire?
83414.e: The lift can get stuck in a fire. That is why you always take the stairs.
83414.m: In a fire, take the stairs, never the lift.

83415.q: Why do you close the door when leaving a room on fire?
a: It holds back smoke and fire
83415.e: A closed door slows down smoke and flames. That way the escape route stays clear for longer.
83415.m: A closed door slows down smoke and fire.

83416.q: What colour are emergency exit signs?
83416.e: Emergency exits and escape routes are marked with green signs. They show a white figure running to a door.

83417.q: What should you not do when escaping from a fire?
83417.e: Looking for things wastes precious time. People are more important than things.
83417.m: In a fire, save yourself, not your toys.

83418.q: Where does everyone meet during a fire drill at school?
83418.e: After leaving the school building, everyone goes to the assembly point. There the teacher can see whether everyone is there.
83418.m: After a fire alarm, everyone meets at the assembly point.

83419.q: Who comes in red vehicles to put out fires?
83419.e: The fire brigade drives red vehicles with blue lights. It puts out fires and rescues people.
83419.m: The fire brigade puts out fires and rescues people.

83420.q: What is barbecue charcoal made from?
83420.e: Barbecue charcoal is charcoal made from wood. Wood is heated with little air until it turns into charcoal.
83420.m: Barbecue charcoal is made from wood.

83421.q: What is the job of people who make charcoal called?
83421.e: Charcoal burners turn wood into charcoal in a big pile. In the Entlebuch in the canton of Lucerne there are still charcoal burners today.

83422.q: What is the big pile of wood in which charcoal burners make charcoal called?
83422.e: In a charcoal kiln, wood is covered with earth. It smoulders there for days with little air and turns into charcoal.
83422.m: In a charcoal kiln, wood turns into charcoal.

83423.q: What must you never pour onto glowing barbecue charcoal?
83423.e: Methylated spirits and petrol evaporate and catch fire explosively. A dangerous jet of flame shoots up.
83423.m: Never pour methylated spirits or petrol onto glowing charcoal.

83424.q: How can you tell that the barbecue charcoal is ready for grilling?
a: It is covered in grey ash
83424.e: When the charcoal is glowing right through, a grey layer lies on it. Then it gives off even heat.
83424.m: Grey charcoal is ready for grilling.

83425.q: Why must you never use a charcoal barbecue in a closed room?
a: The charcoal goes out at once
83425.e: Glowing charcoal produces carbon monoxide. This gas is poisonous and you cannot smell it.
83425.m: A charcoal barbecue belongs outdoors only.

83426.q: What do you use to light barbecue charcoal safely?
83426.e: Firelighters burn slowly and evenly. That way the charcoal lights without a jet of flame.

83427.q: What do you use to turn sausages on a hot barbecue?
83427.e: Barbecue tongs are long and made of metal. That way your fingers stay well away from the embers.

83626.q: You count how many bikes are in front of the school. What are you doing?
83626.e: When you count, measure or ask and write down the result, you are collecting data.
83626.m: Counting and writing it down means collecting data.

83627.q: What is the easiest way to count how many red cars drive past?
83627.e: For each red car you draw a line. At the end you count the lines.
83627.m: With a tally chart you can count quickly and easily.

83628.q: How do you write the number 5 on a tally chart?
a: Four lines and one line across
83628.e: You draw four lines and cross them through with the fifth line. That makes bundles of five.
83628.m: On a tally chart you always bundle five lines.

83629.q: A tally chart shows two bundles of five and three lines. How many is that?
83629.e: Two bundles of five are 10, plus 3 lines. 10 + 3 makes 13.
83629.m: Bundles of five help you add up quickly.

83630.q: What is best for measuring how tall a plant is?
83630.e: You measure lengths with a ruler or tape measure. Then you write down the number.
83630.m: To collect data you need the right measuring tool.

83631.q: What do you use to collect data about the weather, for example the temperature?
83631.e: A thermometer shows how warm or cold it is. You can write down the reading every day.

83632.q: Why do you write down data you have collected?
a: So you do not forget it
83632.e: What you write down you can read again later, compare and analyse.
83632.m: Data that is written down can be looked at again later.

83633.q: Every day you check whether the sun is shining. How long should you do this to get a good overview?
83633.e: The longer you observe, the more data you have. Then you see whether it is often or rarely sunny.

83634.q: Where do you enter numbers you have collected so they are clear?
83634.e: A table has rows and columns. That way you can find each number again quickly.
83634.m: In a table, data stands neatly in rows and columns.

83635.q: What do you write down before you go shopping?
83635.e: On a shopping list you write one below the other what you want to buy. That way you do not forget anything.
83635.m: A shopping list helps you not to forget anything.

83636.q: How are things usually written on a list?
a: Drawn on top of each other
83636.e: On a list you write each item on its own line, one below the other.
83636.m: On a list each item has its own line.

83637.q: What do you call a single thing on a list?
83637.e: Each thing written on the list is an item.
83637.m: A list is made up of single items.

83638.q: Your shopping list has bread, milk, cheese and apples. How many items are there?
83638.e: Bread, milk, cheese and apples are four things, so four items.
83638.m: You can count the items on a list.

83639.q: What do you do with an item on your to-do list when the task is done?
83639.e: With a tick you see straight away what is already done and what is still missing.
83639.m: You tick off finished tasks on the list.

83640.q: Which list shows which children are in the class?
83640.e: The class list has the names of all the children in a class.
83640.m: The class list names all the children in a class.

83641.q: You have a list with 6 names and cross out 2. How many names are left?
83641.e: 6 minus 2 makes 4. Four names are not crossed out yet.

83642.q: What is on a guest list for a party?
83642.e: A guest list shows who is invited to the party.
83642.m: The guest list has all the invited guests.

83643.q: Why do you number the items on a list 1, 2, 3 and so on?
83643.e: With numbers you see straight away how many items there are, and you can name each one exactly.

83644.q: Which name comes first in alphabetical order: Lea, Ben or Mia?
83644.e: You look at the first letter. B comes before L and M.
83644.m: When sorting alphabetically, the first letter counts first.

83646.q: Which letter comes directly before F in the alphabet?
83646.e: The order is C, D, E, F, G. So E comes before F.
83646.m: If you know the alphabet well, you find neighbouring letters quickly.

83647.q: How many letters does the alphabet have?
83647.e: The alphabet goes from A to Z and has 26 letters.

83648.q: Which letter comes directly after M in the alphabet?
83648.e: The order is K, L, M, N, O. So N comes after M.
83648.m: You need to know the alphabet by heart to sort well.

83649.q: Which city comes last in alphabetical order: Bern, Zurich or Lucerne?
83649.e: Z is the last letter of the alphabet. That is why Zurich comes after Bern and Lucerne.
83649.m: Words with Z come right at the end.

83652.q: You have buttons in red, blue and yellow. How can you group them?
83652.e: All the red buttons go together, and so do all the blue and all the yellow ones.
83652.m: When grouping, things that have something in common go together.

83653.q: Which thing does not fit in the group: apple, pear, banana, hammer?
83653.e: Apple, pear and banana are fruit. A hammer is a tool.
83653.m: When you group things, you also see what does not belong.

83654.q: What do a dog, a cat and a rabbit have in common?
83654.e: Dog, cat and rabbit all belong to the group of animals.
83654.m: Things in a group share a feature.

83655.q: You have 12 children and make groups of 3. How many groups are there?
83655.e: 12 divided into groups of 3 makes 4 groups, because 4 · 3 makes 12.
83655.m: To share into equal groups you divide.

83656.q: How can you group building blocks?
83656.e: You can sort building blocks into cubes, cuboids and cylinders, for example.
83656.m: Shapes, colours and sizes are good for grouping.

83657.e: Bike, bus and train are all vehicles. Each of the other groups has something else in it.
83657.m: In a group, all the things go together.

83658.q: When you sort things into groups, what becomes easier?
83658.e: If you know which group something is in, you find it more quickly.

83659.q: Which animal does not fit with the others: eagle, sparrow, blackbird, trout?
83659.e: Eagle, sparrow and blackbird are birds. The trout is a fish.

83660.q: What does a Venn diagram show?
83660.e: In a Venn diagram you draw circles. Into each circle go the things that belong to the same set.
83660.m: A Venn diagram shows groups as circles.

83661.q: How do you usually draw a set in a Venn diagram?
83661.e: A closed line like a circle surrounds all the things that belong to the set.
83661.m: You draw a set with a closed line.

83662.q: One circle is called “red”, another “round”. Where does a red ball go?
83662.e: A red ball is red and round. That is why it belongs in both circles, so in the shared part.
83662.m: Something that belongs to two sets goes in the overlap.

83663.q: A circle is called “animals”. Where does a stone go?
83663.e: A stone is not an animal. That is why it does not belong in the circle “animals”.
83663.m: Something that does not belong to the set goes outside.

83664.q: Circles “can fly” and “has feathers”: where does a duck go?
83664.e: A duck can fly and has feathers. So it goes in the shared part of the two circles.
83664.m: One thing can be in several sets at the same time.

83665.q: Circles “can fly” and “has feathers”: where does a penguin go?
83665.e: A penguin has feathers but cannot fly. That is why it goes only in the circle “has feathers”.

83666.q: The circle “even numbers” contains 2, 4 and 6. Where does 8 go?
83666.e: 8 is an even number, just like 2, 4 and 6. So it goes in the circle.
83666.m: Numbers can also be sorted into sets.

83667.q: The circle “children with a bike” has 5 children, the circle “children with a scooter” has 4. Two children are in both circles. How many children have a bike but no scooter?
83667.e: Of the 5 children with a bike, 2 also have a scooter. 5 minus 2 makes 3.
83667.m: You have to pay attention to the overlap when counting.

83668.q: What does a family tree show?
83668.e: A family tree shows the family: parents, children, grandparents and so on.
83668.m: A family tree shows how a family is related.

83669.q: What do you call your parents' parents?
83669.e: The mother and father of your mother or father are your grandparents.
83669.m: Your parents' parents are your grandparents.

83670.q: What do you call children with the same parents?
83670.m: Brothers and sisters are called siblings.

83671.e: The children of your aunt and uncle are your cousins.
83671.m: The children of your uncle and aunt are your cousins.

83672.q: How many grandparents does a person have?
83672.e: Every person has two parents, and each parent has two parents too. 2 + 2 makes 4.

83673.e: Your parents' sisters are your aunts.
83673.m: Your mother's or father's sister is an aunt.

83674.q: Where in a family tree are the oldest relatives often shown?
83674.e: Often the oldest are at the top and the younger family members below. But some family trees are drawn the other way round.
83674.m: A family tree arranges the family by generations.

83675.q: What do you call the children of your children?
83675.e: For grandparents, the children of their children are their grandchildren.
83675.m: The children of your own children are your grandchildren.

83676.q: What do you need a dictionary for?
a: To look up how to spell a word
83676.e: In a dictionary you find the correct spelling and often the meaning of words too.
83676.m: You look up words in a dictionary.

83677.q: You are looking up “zebra” in a dictionary. Where do you look?
83677.e: Z is the last letter of the alphabet. That is why words with Z are right at the back.
83677.m: You find words with Z at the back of the dictionary.

83678.q: You are looking up “ant” in a dictionary. Where do you look?
83678.e: A is the first letter of the alphabet. Words with A are at the beginning.
83678.m: You find words with A at the front of the dictionary.

83679.q: What are the words at the top of a dictionary page for?
a: They show which words are on the page
They show the colour of the page
83679.e: At the top there is often the first or last word on the page. That way you quickly see whether the word you want is on this page.
83679.m: The guide words at the top show which words are on a page.

83680.q: You are looking for “cat”. The page starts with “camel” and ends with “canoe”. What do you do?
83680.e: In “cat”, t comes after n. So “cat” comes after “canoe”, further back in the dictionary.
83680.m: When looking things up, you compare letter by letter.

83681.q: In which form do you usually find “went” in the dictionary?
83681.e: Verbs are usually listed in their basic form in the dictionary. So for “went” you look up “go”.
83681.m: You look up verbs in the dictionary in their basic form.

83682.q: In which form do you usually find “mice” in the dictionary?
83682.e: Nouns are listed in the singular in the dictionary. For “mice” you look up “mouse”.
83682.m: You look up nouns in the dictionary in the singular.

83683.q: What is the name of a well-known German dictionary that is also used in Swiss schools?
83683.e: The Duden is a well-known dictionary for German spelling.
83683.m: The Duden shows the correct spelling of German words.

a: A list of all the books in the library
83684.e: The catalogue shows which books the library has and where they are.
83684.m: In the library catalogue you find all the books in a library.

83685.q: What can you search for in the library catalogue?
83685.e: You can search by the title of the book, the name of the author or a topic.
83685.m: In the catalogue you search by title, author or topic.

83686.q: What do you usually need to borrow a book from the library?
83686.e: With the card, the library knows who has borrowed the book.
83686.m: You borrow books with a library card.

83687.q: What is the small sticker with letters and numbers on the spine of a book, which shows where the book belongs, called?
83687.e: The shelf mark is like an address. It shows which shelf the book belongs on.
83687.m: The shelf mark shows a book's place on the shelf.

83688.q: How do many libraries search their catalogue today?
83688.e: In the past there were index cards in drawers. Today the catalogue is usually stored on a computer.
83688.m: Today the library catalogue is usually on the computer.

83689.q: What must you do when the loan period of a book is over?
83689.e: Borrowed books belong to the library. After the loan period you take them back so that others can read them too.
83689.m: You return borrowed books on time.

83690.q: What does the catalogue show when a book is currently on loan?
a: That it is not on the shelf
83690.e: The catalogue shows whether a book is available or currently on loan.
83690.m: The catalogue tells you whether a book is there right now.

83691.q: Before there were computers, where was the information about the books written?
83691.e: There was an index card for each book. The cards were kept in order in drawers.
83691.m: In the past a library catalogue was made of lots of index cards.

83692.q: Why do you stick a label on a box?
a: So you know what is inside
83692.e: The label says what is in the box. That way you do not have to open it.
83692.m: A label shows what is in a box.

83693.q: What is often written on the label on your exercise book?
83693.e: With your name and the subject, everyone knows straight away whose book it is and what it is for.
83693.m: The label on an exercise book shows name and subject.

83694.q: What is on the label of a yoghurt in the shop?
a: The use-by date and the ingredients
83694.e: Food packaging shows, for example, the ingredients and when you should eat it by.
83694.m: Labels in the shop show important information about the goods.

83695.q: A jar says “Sugar”, but there is salt inside. What is wrong?
83695.e: A label must match what is inside. Otherwise it is misleading.
83695.m: A label must always match what is inside.

83696.q: What does the label in your T-shirt often show?
83696.e: The label in clothes shows, for example, the size and how to wash them.
83696.m: Clothes labels show size and care.

83697.q: The boxes in the classroom have labels: “Pens”, “Scissors”, “Glue”. Where do you put a pair of scissors?
83697.e: The label shows what belongs in the box. Scissors belong in the box “Scissors”.
83697.m: Labels help you put things away in the right place.

83698.q: What on a label helps children who cannot read yet?
83698.e: A picture, for example of a pen, shows what is in the box even without reading.
83698.m: You can understand pictures on labels without reading.

83699.q: What is on a label on a suitcase at the airport?
a: Where the suitcase is travelling to
83699.e: The luggage label shows the destination. That way the suitcase is loaded onto the right plane.
83699.m: A luggage label gets the suitcase to the right destination.

83700.q: Which category does the tulip belong to?
83700.e: The tulip is a flower. That is why it belongs to the category flowers.
83700.m: A category groups similar things under one name.

83701.q: Which category does the guitar belong to?
83701.e: You make music with a guitar. It belongs to the musical instruments.
83701.m: Musical instruments form their own category.

83702.q: Which word is the name of a category?
83702.e: Carrot, leek and pea are single things. Vegetables is the general term, so the category.
83702.m: The name of a category is a general term.

83703.e: You put on a jumper. Plate, scissors and spoon are not clothes.
83703.m: Clothes are everything you put on.

83704.q: What does NOT belong in the category “furniture”?
83704.e: Table, chair and wardrobe are furniture. A banana is a fruit.
83704.m: Not everything fits into every category.

83705.q: In which category do you find a book about dinosaurs in the library?
83705.e: A book that explains real facts about dinosaurs is a non-fiction book.
83705.m: Books with real facts belong to non-fiction.

83706.q: Which category does orange juice belong to?
83706.e: You drink orange juice. That is why it belongs to drinks.
83706.m: Everything you drink belongs to the category drinks.

83707.q: Why are there categories in the shop like “bread”, “dairy” or “vegetables”?
83707.e: When similar goods are together, you know where to look.
83707.m: Categories help you find things quickly.

83708.q: What is in a fact file about an animal?
a: Important facts like size and food
83708.e: A fact file contains short, important facts, for example name, size, habitat and food.
83708.m: A fact file sums up important facts briefly.

83709.q: What belongs in a fact file about you?
83709.e: A personal fact file has details like name, age, hobbies and favourite food.
83709.m: A fact file about you has your name and age.

83710.q: How are the facts in a fact file usually written?
83710.e: You should be able to read a fact file quickly. That is why you write short key words one below the other.
83710.m: A fact file is short and clear.

83711.q: Which fact fits under “Food” in a squirrel's fact file?
83711.e: Squirrels like to eat nuts, seeds and buds. The other words describe something else, for example the colour or the size.
83711.m: Each fact belongs under the right heading.

83712.q: What is often shown on a fact file as well?
83712.e: A photo or drawing shows straight away what the animal or person looks like.
83712.m: A picture makes a fact file clearer.

83713.q: Which detail should you NOT write in a fact file that is on the internet?
83713.e: Your address is private. Strangers should not know where you live.
83713.m: Private details like my address do not belong on the internet.

83714.q: A fact file says: “lives in water, has fins, breathes with gills”. Which animal is it?
83714.e: Fish have fins and gills. With them they can swim and breathe in water.
83714.m: With a good fact file you can recognise an animal.

83715.q: Under which heading in an animal fact file does “forest” go?
83715.e: The habitat says where an animal lives, for example in the forest, in water or in a meadow.
83715.m: The habitat shows where an animal is at home.

83716.q: In the past, what did the police use wanted posters describing a person for?
a: To find people they were looking for
83716.e: In the past the police searched for people with wanted posters. They showed what the person looked like and their features.
83716.m: A description like this lets people recognise someone.

83717.q: What do you do in a survey?
a: Ask lots of people the same thing
Read a book on your own
83717.e: In a survey you ask several people the same question and collect the answers.
83717.m: In a survey you ask lots of people the same thing.

83718.q: Which question is good for a survey in the class?
a: How many legs does a dog have?
83718.e: With this question, each child gives a different answer. The other questions have only one correct answer.
83718.m: A good survey question can be answered in different ways.

83719.q: In a survey, 8 children say “pizza”, 5 “spaghetti” and 3 “soup”. What is the most popular?
83719.e: Pizza has the most answers, with 8 votes.
83719.m: The answer with the most votes is the most popular.

83720.q: In a survey, 8 children say “pizza”, 5 “spaghetti” and 3 “soup”. How many children were asked?
83720.e: 8 + 5 + 3 makes 16. That is how many children answered.
83720.m: If you add up all the answers, you know how many took part.

83721.q: What is a good way to show the results of a survey?
83721.e: In a bar chart each bar is as tall as the number of votes. That way you see straight away what is most common.
83721.m: A bar chart shows survey results at a glance.

83722.q: What is important in a survey?
a: You only ask your best friends
Whoever answers first gets two votes
83722.e: If someone counts more than once or only friends are asked, the result is no longer right.
83722.m: In a fair survey each vote counts only once.

83723.q: In a survey, the bars are 6 for “cat” and 9 for “dog”. How many more votes does “dog” have?
83723.e: 9 minus 6 makes 3. So the dog has 3 more votes.
83723.m: You find differences in a chart by subtracting.

83724.q: What must you NOT do in a survey?
83724.e: The answers must stay exactly as people gave them. Otherwise the survey is wrong.
83724.m: You always report survey answers honestly.

83725.q: How can you vote quickly in a class survey?
a: You send each child a letter
83725.e: Everyone who chooses an answer raises their hand. Then you count the hands.
83725.m: You can vote quickly by raising your hand.

83925.q: Where do many people sweat especially heavily?
83925.e: There are many sweat glands under the arms, and the skin is pressed closely together there. That is why your armpits quickly get damp during sport.
83925.m: You sweat especially heavily under your arms.

83926.e: There is some salt dissolved in sweat. That is why it tastes salty.
83926.m: Sweat tastes salty because there is salt in it.

83927.q: What is sweat mainly made of?
83927.e: Sweat is almost all water. There is also a little salt and other substances.

83928.q: What should you do if you sweat a lot during sport?
83928.e: When you sweat, your body loses water. You have to drink this water again.
83928.m: If you sweat a lot, you need to drink enough.

83929.q: When do you usually sweat the most?
a: When running on a hot day
83929.e: In the heat and when moving, the body gets warm. Then it sweats especially a lot.
83929.m: Heat and exercise make us sweat.

83930.q: What do the sweat glands in your skin make?
83930.e: Sweat glands are in the skin. They release sweat to the outside through tiny openings.

83931.q: Why does sweat smell unpleasant after a while?
a: Because of bacteria on the skin
83931.e: Fresh sweat hardly smells at all. Only when bacteria on the skin break it down does it start to smell.
83931.m: Bacteria cause the smell of sweat.

83932.q: How does sweat cool the skin?
83932.e: When sweat evaporates, it takes heat away from the skin. That way the skin cools down.

83933.q: Where does sweat come out of the skin?
83933.e: The skin has lots and lots of tiny openings, the pores. Sweat comes out there.
83933.m: Sweat comes out of tiny pores.

a: Small brown dots on the skin
83934.e: Freckles are small, light brown spots. They do not hurt.

83935.q: Why can you see freckles better in summer?
a: Because they get darker in summer
83935.e: Because of the sun, the skin makes more brown pigment. That is why the dots are easier to see in summer.

83936.q: Where do you often see freckles?
a: On the soles of the feet
83936.e: Freckles appear where a lot of sun shines on the skin. The face gets a particularly large amount of sun.
83936.m: Freckles are often on the face.

83937.q: Which people have freckles especially often?
a: People with fair skin and red hair
83937.e: Freckles are seen mainly on very fair skin. Red-haired people have them especially often.

83938.e: Freckles are small spots of colour. They are not an illness and not catching.

83939.q: Where does the tendency to have freckles come from?
a: It is inherited from your parents
83939.e: Whether you get freckles is inherited. That is why several people in one family often have them.
83939.m: The tendency to have freckles is inherited.

83940.q: What helps stop freckles getting even darker?
83940.e: Sunlight makes freckles darker. Sun cream and a hat protect the skin.

83941.q: What do freckles feel like when you run your finger over them?
a: Flat like the rest of the skin
83941.e: Freckles are just colour in the skin. That is why you cannot feel them; they are completely flat.
83941.m: Freckles are flat and you cannot feel them.

83942.e: A mole is a spot with lots of pigment cells. It is usually harmless.
83942.m: A mole is usually a harmless spot.

83943.q: What is another name for a mole?
83943.e: Mole and beauty spot usually mean the same thing. It is just a small coloured spot on the skin.
83943.m: A mole is also called a beauty spot.

83944.q: What should you do if a mole changes a lot?
83944.e: If a mole grows, itches or bleeds, a doctor should look at it. That way she can check whether everything is all right.
83944.m: Show changed moles to a doctor.

83945.q: Which change in a mole should you take seriously?
83945.e: A mole that grows quickly should be checked. Small, round moles that stay the same are usually harmless.
83945.m: Have a quickly growing mole checked.

83946.q: What is the doctor called who knows all about the skin?
83946.e: The dermatologist looks after the skin. She can also examine moles closely.
83946.m: The dermatologist looks after the skin.

83947.q: Can you wash off a mole?
a: No, it is in the skin
83947.e: The colour of a mole is inside the skin. That is why you cannot wash it off.
83947.m: You cannot wash off a mole.

83948.e: Most moles are light to dark brown. They contain a lot of brown pigment.

83949.q: Can new moles appear during your life?
a: Yes, especially in children and teenagers
83949.e: Many moles only appear during childhood and the teenage years. The sun can also play a part.

83950.q: What is often inside an inflamed spot?
83950.e: An inflamed spot often has a whitish dot. That is pus.
83950.m: There is often pus in an inflamed spot.

83951.q: Why should you not squeeze spots?
a: It can cause inflammation and scars
83951.e: Squeezing pushes germs deeper into the skin. Then it can get worse and leave marks.
83951.m: It is better not to squeeze spots.

83952.q: What can block the tiny holes in the skin so that a spot forms?
83952.e: The skin makes its own oil. If too much of it blocks a tiny hole in the skin, a spot can form.
83952.m: Too much skin oil can cause spots.

83953.q: Where do you get spots especially often?
a: On the soles of the feet
83953.e: The skin on the face has many glands that make skin oil. That is why spots appear there especially often.
83953.m: Spots often appear on the face.

83954.q: Who gets lots of spots especially often?
83954.e: In teenagers, the skin makes especially large amounts of skin oil. That is why many people of this age have spots.

83955.q: What is the skin condition with very many spots called?
83955.e: With acne, you have lots of spots, often on the face and back. A doctor can help with it.
83955.m: Acne is a skin condition with lots of spots.

83956.q: What is good for the skin when you have spots?
83956.e: Gentle washing removes extra oil and dirt. Scratching and rubbing only irritate the skin.
83956.m: With spots, wash your skin gently.

83957.q: What usually happens to a spot after a few days?
83957.e: Most spots disappear by themselves after a few days. The body heals them itself.

83958.q: How do you often get a graze?
83958.e: When you fall, your skin rubs over the rough ground. The top layer of skin is scraped off.
83958.m: When you fall, you often graze your skin.

83959.q: What do you do first with a dirty graze?
83959.e: First the dirt has to come out of the wound. To do this, you rinse it with clean water.

83960.q: What do you stick on a small graze?
83960.e: A plaster protects the wound from dirt. It has a soft pad in the middle.

83961.q: What forms on a graze when it heals?
83961.e: Dried blood and wound fluid form a hard crust. This crust is called a scab.
83961.m: A scab forms on a healing wound.

83962.q: Why should you not pick off the scab on a wound?
83962.e: New skin grows under the scab. If you pick it off, you disturb the healing.
83962.m: The scab protects the wound while it heals.

83963.q: Which part of the body is mainly injured in a graze?
83963.e: In a graze, only the top layer of skin is rubbed off. That is why it usually only bleeds a little.
83963.m: A graze injures the top layer of skin.

83964.q: What protects your knees from grazes when inline skating?
83964.e: Knee pads are hard pads over the knees. If you fall, the pad slides over the ground instead of your skin.
83964.m: Knee pads protect your knees when you fall.

83965.q: What can make a graze inflamed?
83965.e: If dirt and germs get into the wound, it can become inflamed. Then it goes red, warm and hurts more.
83965.m: Dirt and germs can make a wound inflamed.

83966.q: Where do children especially often get grazes when they fall?
83966.e: When you fall, you often catch yourself with your knees and arms. That is why knees and elbows are often grazed.
83966.m: Knees and elbows are often grazed.

83967.q: Which pet can scratch with its claws?
83967.e: Cats have sharp claws. When they defend themselves or play, they can scratch.
83967.m: Cats can scratch with their claws.

83968.q: What can easily give you a scratch on the hand when picking berries?
83968.e: Brambles have lots of small prickles. They easily scratch the skin.
83968.m: Thorny brambles can scratch the skin.

83969.q: What should you do after a cat scratch?
83969.e: Even a small scratch can contain germs. That is why you clean the spot well with soap and water.

83970.q: How can you stop yourself scratching until you bleed?
83970.e: Short fingernails are less sharp. That way you injure your skin less when you scratch.

a: A small, long injury to the skin
A round mark under the skin
A thick, hard patch of skin
83971.e: In a scratch, something sharp scrapes the skin open. That is why it is usually narrow and long.
83971.m: A scratch is a narrow scrape wound.

83972.q: Why should you not scratch an itchy spot until it bleeds?
a: Germs can get into the skin
83972.e: Scratching opens the skin. Then germs can get in and make the spot inflamed.
83972.m: Scratching until it bleeds lets germs in.

83973.q: Does a small, shallow scratch usually heal with or without a scar?
83973.e: In a small scratch, only the top layer of skin is injured. It usually grows back without a trace.
83973.m: Small scratches usually heal without a trace.

83974.q: What do people usually scratch themselves with?
83974.e: Fingernails are hard and have an edge. You use them to scratch yourself when you itch.
83974.m: We scratch ourselves with our fingernails.

a: From a knock or a blow
83975.e: When you knock yourself, the tissue under the skin is squashed. Afterwards you see a dark mark.
83975.m: A knock can cause a bruise.

83976.q: What has happened under the skin with a bruise?
83976.e: The knock tears tiny blood vessels. A little blood runs into the tissue and shows dark through the skin.
83976.m: Under a bruise, a little blood has leaked out.

83977.q: What is another word for a bruise?
83977.e: Haematoma is another word for a bruise. It often hurts a little when you press on it.
83977.m: A bruise is also called a haematoma.

83978.q: Which colours can a bruise turn as it heals?
83978.e: The body slowly breaks down the blood. As it does, the bruise changes colour through green to yellow.
83978.m: A healing bruise turns green and yellow.

83979.q: What helps against a bruise straight after a knock?
a: Bathing the spot in hot water
83979.e: Cold makes the blood vessels narrower. Then less blood leaks out and the bruise stays smaller.
83979.m: Cooling helps straight after a knock.

83980.q: Roughly how long does it take for a bruise to disappear?
83980.e: The body needs time to break down the blood. A bruise has usually gone after one to two weeks.
83980.m: A bruise disappears after about two weeks.

83981.q: Where do children get bruises especially often?
83981.e: On the shin, the bone lies directly under the skin. If you bump into something, you quickly get a bruise there.
83981.m: Bruises quickly appear on the shins.

83982.q: What do you call a swelling on the head after a knock?
83982.e: After a knock, the spot on the head swells up. A round swelling like this is called a bump.
83982.m: After a knock on the head, you often get a bump.

a: A place where a wound has healed
A brown dot from the sun
83983.e: When a wound heals, the body makes new tissue. Afterwards you can see this place as a scar.
83983.m: A scar is a healed wound.

83984.q: When is a scar more likely to be left behind?
83984.e: With deep wounds, the skin cannot grow back exactly the same. Then a scar is left.

83985.q: What colour is a fresh scar often?
83985.e: A fresh scar has a good blood supply. That is why it looks reddish at first.

83986.q: What does a scar usually become like over time?
83986.e: Over the months, a scar gets less blood. It becomes paler and flatter.

83987.q: Does hair grow on a scar?
a: Yes, but only after a year
83987.e: Scar tissue has no hair roots. That is why hair usually does not grow there.
83987.m: Hair usually does not grow on scars.

83988.q: Why should you protect a fresh scar from the sun?
a: So it does not turn dark
83988.e: Fresh scar tissue is sensitive to the sun. Otherwise it can turn brownish.
83988.m: Protect fresh scars from the sun.

83989.q: What helps a deep cut heal nicely?
83989.e: Stitching holds the edges of the wound together. Then only a narrow scar is left.

83990.q: How long does a scar usually last?
83990.e: Scar tissue never completely disappears. It can become paler, but usually stays visible.

83991.q: What is the pigment called that colours the skin brown?
83991.e: Special cells in the skin make melanin. The more of it there is, the darker the skin.

83992.q: What colour does fair skin go with sunburn?
83992.e: With sunburn, the skin is inflamed. It goes red, hot and sore.

83993.q: Why do people have different skin colours?
a: Their skin makes different amounts of pigment
They wash a different number of times
They sleep for different lengths of time
83993.e: How much pigment the skin makes is inherited. This results in many different skin tones.
83993.m: Skin colour depends on the pigment in the skin.

83994.q: What does dark skin protect against better than fair skin?
83994.e: Lots of pigment in the skin blocks some of the sun’s rays. That is why dark skin gets sunburnt less often.
83994.m: Dark skin is better protected from the sun.

83995.q: What do you call the brown colour of the skin after days in the sun?
83995.e: In the sun, the skin makes more pigment to protect itself. This makes it go brown.
83995.m: In the sun, the skin gets a suntan.

83996.q: At what time of day is the summer sun strongest for the skin?
83996.e: Around midday, the sun is at its highest. Then its rays are strongest, so you look for shade.
83996.m: In summer, look for shade around midday.

83997.q: What is it called when your face goes red with embarrassment?
83997.e: When you are embarrassed, more blood flows into your cheeks. That is why your face goes red.
83997.m: People who are embarrassed often blush.

83998.q: What does the skin often look like when you are ill or get a big fright?
83998.e: With a fright or illness, less blood flows through the skin. Then it looks pale.
83998.m: With a fright, the skin often goes pale.

a: Lines and furrows in the skin
83999.e: Wrinkles are lines where the skin folds. You see them on the forehead, for example.
83999.m: Wrinkles are lines in the skin.

84000.q: Why does the skin get wrinkles in old age?
84000.e: Young skin is firm and springs back. In old age it becomes less elastic, so wrinkles stay.

84001.q: What happens to your fingers when you stay in the bath for a long time?
84001.e: After a long bath, the fingertips get lots of little wrinkles. This soon goes away after drying off.
84001.m: After a long bath, your fingers go wrinkly.

84002.q: What is another name for fine wrinkles at the outer corner of the eye?
84002.e: The fine lines at the corner of the eye spread out like a bird’s toes. That is why they are called crow’s feet.
84002.m: Fine lines at the corner of the eye are called crow’s feet.

84003.q: What makes the skin get wrinkly faster?
84003.e: Strong sun damages the skin over time. Then it gets wrinkles earlier.
84003.m: Too much sun makes the skin wrinkly faster.

84004.q: What are the vertical lines between the eyebrows called?
84004.e: When you look cross, you pull your eyebrows together. This creates vertical lines between them.
84004.m: Frown lines are between the eyebrows.

84005.q: Who usually has the most wrinkles on their face?
84005.e: The older a person is, the more wrinkles they usually have. Children have hardly any wrinkles.

84006.q: Which animal is known for its thick, wrinkly skin?
84006.e: An elephant’s skin has lots of deep furrows. Water and mud stay in them, which cools it down.

84007.q: What often forms on a toe when a shoe presses on it for a long time?
84007.e: A corn is a small, hard thickening of hard skin. It forms from pressure, for example from shoes that are too tight.
84007.m: Tight shoes can cause a corn.

84008.q: Why does the skin form hard skin?
a: To protect itself from lots of pressure and rubbing
84008.e: Where the skin is often pressed and rubbed, it makes itself thicker. That way it protects itself.
84008.m: Hard skin protects the skin from lots of pressure.

84009.q: What helps keep hard skin on the feet soft?
a: Wearing shoes that are too tight
84009.e: Foot cream gives the skin moisture and oil. Then the hard skin stays softer.

84010.q: Is hard skin on the feet dangerous?
a: No, it is usually natural protection
Yes, it bleeds all the time
84010.e: Hard skin is thick, firm skin. Normally it protects the foot and is completely natural.
84010.m: Hard skin is usually natural protection.

84011.q: What does hard skin feel like?
84011.e: Hard skin is made of many layers of firm skin cells. That is why it feels hard and rough.
84011.m: Hard skin is hard and rough.

84012.q: What can you use to gently rub off thick hard skin on your feet?
84012.e: A pumice stone is a light, rough stone. You can use it to carefully rub off hard skin.
84012.m: You rub off hard skin with a pumice stone.

84013.q: What do you call a patch of hard skin on the hands, for example from rowing?
84013.e: When hands often grip tightly, hard skin forms there. These hard patches are called calluses.
84013.m: Hard patches on the hands are called calluses.

84014.q: Why can you feel less through thick hard skin?
a: It is made of dead skin cells
84014.e: Hard skin is made of cells that are no longer alive. That is why you feel less there.
84014.m: Hard skin is made of dead cells.

84015.q: What can develop with very thick, dry hard skin on the heel?
84015.e: Very thick, dry hard skin is no longer bendy. It can split open, and that hurts.
84015.m: Hard skin that is too thick can crack.

84016.q: Why does a mosquito bite itch?
84016.e: When it bites, the mosquito puts a little saliva into the skin. The body reacts to it, and it itches.
84016.m: The mosquito’s saliva causes the itching.

84017.e: Only the females bite. They need blood so that their eggs can grow.

84018.q: When do mosquitoes especially like to bite in our part of the world?
a: In the evening and at night
84018.e: Many mosquitoes are out and about at dusk and at night. That is why they often buzz around as you fall asleep.
84018.m: Mosquitoes often bite in the evening and at night.

84019.q: Where do mosquitoes lay their eggs?
84019.e: Mosquito larvae live in water. That is why the females lay their eggs on or near water, for example in ponds, puddles or water butts.
84019.m: Mosquitoes lay their eggs on or next to water.

84020.q: What helps against the itching of a mosquito bite?
84020.e: Cold calms the skin, and the itching gets less. Scratching, on the other hand, only makes it worse.

84021.q: What protects you from mosquito bites at night?
84021.e: A mosquito net hangs over the bed like a fine tent. The mosquitoes cannot get through.
84021.m: A mosquito net keeps mosquitoes away.

84022.q: What does a mosquito bite usually look like?
84022.e: After the bite, the skin swells up a little at that spot. It goes red and itches.
84022.m: A mosquito bite is a small red swelling.

84023.q: What attracts mosquitoes to us humans?
84023.e: Mosquitoes smell the air we breathe out and our body smell. That way they find us even in the dark.
84023.m: Mosquitoes find us by our breath and smell.

84024.q: What does a mosquito bite with?
a: With a sting on its rear end
84024.e: The mosquito has a thin tube-like mouthpart on its head. It uses it to pierce the skin and suck.
84024.m: The mosquito bites with its mouthpart.

84222.q: What does the term climate change mean?
a: The Earth's climate changes over a long time
The weather changes from one day to the next
84222.e: In climate change, the typical weather changes over many decades. Today the Earth is mainly getting warmer.
84222.m: Climate change means that the climate changes over a long time.

84223.q: Because of today's climate change, is the Earth getting warmer or colder on average?
84223.e: The Earth's average temperature has risen clearly over the last 150 years. That is why people also speak of global warming.
84223.m: Climate change is making the Earth warmer.

84224.q: Which human activity contributes especially strongly to climate change?
84224.e: Burning coal, oil and gas produces exhaust gases that hold heat in the air. This makes it warmer.
84224.m: Burning coal, oil and gas heats up the climate.

84226.q: What is an especially climate-friendly way to get to school?
84226.e: Walking or cycling produces no exhaust gases. It also keeps you fit.
84226.m: Walking or cycling is good for the climate.

84227.q: Because of climate change, what is happening to snow at low altitudes in Switzerland?
a: There is the same amount of snow
84227.e: Because it is warmer, rain falls more often instead of snow on the Central Plateau. Many low-lying ski areas are also short of snow.
84227.m: There is less snow in the lowlands today than in the past.

84228.q: Why do trees help against climate change?
a: They take carbon dioxide out of the air
84228.e: Trees need carbon dioxide to grow and store it in their wood. That way less of it stays in the air.
84228.m: Trees take carbon dioxide out of the air.

84229.q: How are heatwaves in Switzerland changing because of climate change?
a: They only come in winter now
84229.e: Because it is getting warmer overall, there are more very hot days. Heatwaves therefore happen more often and get stronger.
84229.m: With climate change there are more heatwaves.

84230.q: How can you save energy at home and so help the climate?
a: Switch off the light when you leave the room
Leave the windows open in winter
Leave the TV on all the time
84230.e: Electricity and heating use energy. If you switch off lights you do not need, you save energy.

84231.q: What are parts of the Rhône Glacier covered with in summer so that it melts more slowly?
84231.e: The white sheets reflect the sunlight. Underneath them the ice melts more slowly.
84231.m: White sheets protect the ice from the sun.

84232.q: Why are the glaciers in the Alps melting?
a: Because the wind is getting stronger
84232.e: In a warmer climate, more ice melts in summer than is added by snow in winter. That is why the glaciers are getting smaller.

84233.q: Where does the meltwater of a glacier flow?
84233.e: The meltwater gathers into streams. These flow into rivers such as the Rhône or the Rhine.
84233.m: Meltwater from glaciers flows into streams and rivers.

84234.q: What often forms where a glacier has melted away?
84234.e: Meltwater collects in the hollow that the ice leaves behind. This is how new glacier lakes form.
84234.m: Where a glacier disappears, a lake often forms.

84235.q: Why does ice covered in dark dust melt faster?
a: Dark surfaces absorb more heat from the sun
84235.e: Dark surfaces absorb more sunlight and so get warmer. That is why dirty ice melts faster.
84235.m: Dark surfaces get warmer in the sun than light ones.

84236.q: Which canton is the Great Aletsch Glacier in?
84236.e: The Great Aletsch Glacier is in Upper Valais. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
84236.m: The Aletsch Glacier is in Valais.

84237.q: In which season does the most glacier ice melt?
84237.e: In summer it is warm even in the mountains. That is when the most meltwater flows out of the glacier.

84238.q: What will be missing in high summer later on, once the glaciers have disappeared?
84238.e: Glaciers release a lot of water, especially in hot, dry summers. Without them, some rivers will then carry less water.
84238.m: Glaciers are important stores of water for the summer.

a: Several very hot days in a row
A high wave in the sea
A warm wind in the evening
84239.e: In a heatwave it stays very hot for several days. Often the nights hardly cool down either.
84239.m: A heatwave is lots of hot days in a row.

84240.q: What should you definitely do in great heat?
a: Run about in the sun at midday
84240.e: In heat, your body sweats out a lot of water. That is why you need to drink regularly, even if you are not thirsty.
84240.m: In hot weather, drink lots of water.

84241.q: Where was Switzerland's highest temperature, 41.5 °C in 2003, measured?
84241.e: On 11 August 2003, 41.5 °C was measured in Grono in the Misox valley. That is still the Swiss record today (as of 2026).
84241.m: The Swiss heat record comes from Grono.

84242.q: What is a day called when the temperature reaches at least 30 °C?
84242.e: From 30 °C, it is called a hot day. A summer day, on the other hand, only needs 25 °C.
84242.m: On a hot day it reaches at least 30 degrees.

84243.q: What is a night called when it does not cool down below 20 °C?
84243.e: On a tropical night it stays as warm as in the tropics. Many people sleep badly then.
84243.m: On a tropical night it stays above 20 degrees.

84244.q: Who is especially at risk during a heatwave?
84244.e: The bodies of babies and older people are less able to cool down. They need special attention in hot weather.
84244.m: Babies and older people need special protection in hot weather.

84245.q: On a hot summer's day, when is it usually hottest outside?
84245.e: The sun heats the ground and the air all day long. That is why it usually gets warmest in the afternoon.
84245.m: It is usually hottest outside in the afternoon.

84246.q: How do you keep a flat cool during the day in hot weather?
a: Open all the windows in the midday sun
84246.e: Closed shutters keep the sun out. It is best to air the rooms in the cool night or early morning.
84246.m: In hot weather, keep the shutters closed during the day.

84247.q: Which clothes are best in great heat?
84247.e: Light fabrics let air reach your skin, and pale colours heat up less. A hat also protects your head.
84247.m: In hot weather, wear light, pale clothes.

a: A long time with too little rain
84248.e: In a drought it rains too little for weeks or months. The soil, plants and rivers and lakes dry out.
84248.m: In a drought there is no rain for a long time.

84249.q: What do you often see in the ground during a drought?
84249.e: When the soil dries out, it shrinks. This makes cracks.
84249.m: In dry weather, the ground cracks.

84250.q: Why are fires in the forest often banned in very dry weather?
a: Because a forest fire can start quickly
Because the trees are asleep then
Because otherwise it starts to rain
Because the foresters are on holiday
84250.e: Dry leaves and grass burn very easily. One spark can start a big forest fire.
84250.m: In dry weather, do not light fires in the forest.

84251.q: In the drought summer of 2018, how did some cows on Swiss alpine pastures get water?
a: The army flew it in by helicopter
They licked ice from the glaciers
They drank milk instead of water
84251.e: Because springs dried up, the Swiss Army flew water up to alpine pastures by helicopter. That way the animals had enough to drink.
84251.m: In summer 2018 the army flew water to the cows.

84252.q: What happens to the plants in the fields during a drought?
84252.e: Plants need water to live. Without rain they wilt and the harvest is small.

84253.q: What happens to the water in rivers and lakes during a long dry spell?
84253.e: Without rain, less water flows in. That is why rivers and lakes get lower.
84253.m: In dry weather the water level drops.
